SEC-KV-NET-004-RC06.desc: Believing that "Protected Mode" is a performance throttle rather than a security control.

SEC-KV-NET-004-RC07.name: Automated Script Failure
SEC-KV-NET-004-RC07.desc: Deployment scripts failing due to protected mode prompts, resolved by `CONFIG SET protected-mode no`.

SEC-KV-NET-005-RC01.name: Flat Network Topology
SEC-KV-NET-005-RC01.desc: Legacy "DMZ" style networks where app servers and databases share the same subnet.

SEC-KV-NET-005-RC02.name: Cost Savings
SEC-KV-NET-005-RC02.desc: Using a single subnet to avoid paying for multiple NAT Gateways or complex VPC peering/Transit Gateway charges.

SEC-KV-NET-005-RC03.name: Complexity Aversion
SEC-KV-NET-005-RC03.desc: Avoiding the complexity of managing CIDR blocks, route tables, and NACLs.

SEC-KV-NET-005-RC04.name: Lift and Shift
SEC-KV-NET-005-RC04.desc: Migrating on-premise workloads directly to the cloud without refactoring for VPC segmentation.

SEC-KV-NET-005-RC05.name: Shared Resources
SEC-KV-NET-005-RC05.desc: Sharing a database instance across multiple environments (Dev, Test, Prod) residing in different networks.

SEC-KV-NET-005-RC06.name: PaaS Limitations
SEC-KV-NET-005-RC06.desc: Using platform-as-a-service offerings that default to rootcause endpoints unless "Private Link" is explicitly paid for/configured.

SEC-KV-NET-005-RC07.name: Microservices Anti-pattern
SEC-KV-NET-005-RC07.desc: Microservices requiring direct database access across different clusters/regions without proper tunneling.

SEC-KV-NET-005-RC08.name: Default VPC Usage
SEC-KV-NET-005-RC08.desc: Deploying resources into the default AWS/Cloud provider VPC which typically has rootcause subnets pre-configured.

SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC01.name: Performance Concerns
SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC01.desc: Belief that TLS adds unacceptable latency or CPU overhead to high-throughput key-value operations.

SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC02.name: Legacy Client Libraries
SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC02.desc: Application drivers or client libraries being too old to support TLS natively.

SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC03.name: Certificate Management Complexity
SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC03.desc: Lack of automated PKI/Cert rotation infrastructure (e.g., Cert-Manager, ACM) making TLS hard to maintain.

SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC04.name: Internal Trust
SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC04.desc: "The network is trusted" fallacy—assuming private VPC traffic is safe from sniffing.

SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC05.name: Default Configuration
SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC05.desc: Most KV stores (historically Redis, Memcached) default to plaintext for backward compatibility.

SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC06.name: Debugging Difficulty
SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC06.desc: Disabling TLS to make packet capture (Wireshark/tcpdump) easier for troubleshooting.

SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC07.name: Complexity
SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC07.desc: TLS setup in KV stores often requires sidecars (stunnel) or complex flag combinations compared to HTTP servers.

SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC08.name: Development Parity
SEC-KV-ENC-001-RC08.desc: Dev environment uses plaintext; configuration accidentally promoted to Prod.

SEC-KV-ENC-002-RC01.name: Outdated Defaults
SEC-KV-ENC-002-RC01.desc: Using default cipher suites provided by the OS or DB version which may include TLS 1.0/1.1 or RC4/DES.

SEC-KV-ENC-002-RC06.name: Lack of Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS)
SEC-KV-ENC-002-RC06.desc: Not prioritizing ECDHE cipher suites in the configuration.

SEC-KV-ENC-002-RC07.name: Certificate Validation Disabled
SEC-KV-ENC-002-RC07.desc: Clients configured with `InsecureSkipVerify` or `ssl_cert_reqs=none`, rendering the strength of the cipher irrelevant (Man-in-the-Middle risk).

SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC01.name: Performance Impact
SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC01.desc: Fear of IOPS latency degradation due to disk encryption overhead.

SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC02.name: Feature Availability
SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC02.desc: Feature gating (encryption at rest often requires Enterprise versions for self-hosted DBs).

SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC03.name: Lost Opportunity
SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC03.desc: ElastiCache/RDS encryption must often be enabled *at creation time*. If missed, it requires a full migration/re-creation.

SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC04.name: Key Management Overhead
SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC04.desc: Dreading the complexity of managing KMS keys, rotation, and policies.

SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC05.name: Ephemeral Data Misconception
SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC05.desc: Belief that "it's just a cache" so data persistence/security doesn't matter (ignoring PII in session data).

SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC06.name: Storage Layer Reliance
SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC06.desc: Assuming SAN/EBS level encryption is sufficient (or assuming it's on when it's off).

SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC07.name: Backup Negligence
SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC07.desc: Encrypting the live DB volume but dumping unencrypted snapshots/RDB files to S3/Disk.

SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC08.name: OS Compatibility
SEC-KV-ENC-003-RC08.desc: Older Linux kernels lacking hardware support for AES-NI, making encryption slow.

SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC01.name: Mixed Content
SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC01.desc: Encrypting external traffic but leaving inter-node (cluster replication/gossip) traffic in plaintext.

SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC02.name: Termination at Load Balancer
SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC02.desc: Terminating TLS at the load balancer/proxy and sending plaintext to the backend DB (common in private VPCs).

SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC03.name: Incomplete Client Config
SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC03.desc: Updating the server to require TLS but failing to update all microservices, leading to fallback to plaintext ports.

SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC04.name: Monitoring Agents
SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC04.desc: Sidecars or monitoring agents connecting via localhost in plaintext to scrape metrics.

SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC06.name: Certificate Expiry
SEC-KV-ENC-004-RC06.desc: TLS disabled temporarily to mitigate an outage caused by expired certificates, then never re-enabled.

SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC01.name: Key Deletion
SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC01.desc: Accidental deletion of the CMK (Customer Master Key) in AWS KMS/Vault, rendering data permanently inaccessible.

SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC02.name: Key Policy Misconfiguration
SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC02.desc: IAM policy updates accidentally removing the database service's permission to `Decrypt` or `GenerateDataKey`.

SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC03.name: Rotation Failures
SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC03.desc: Automatic key rotation enabled but the application/database doesn't support the new key version immediately.

SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC04.name: Regional Mismatch
SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC04.desc: Creating a key in `us-east-1` and trying to use it for a DB in `us-west-2`.

SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC05.name: Disabled Keys
SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC05.desc: Administrator disabling a key suspecting compromise, causing immediate outage for the DB.

SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC06.name: Alias Confusion
SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC06.desc: Referencing keys by Alias in code/config, then changing the Alias target without updating the DB config.

SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC07.name: Quota Limits
SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC07.desc: Exceeding KMS request quotas due to high-throughput database operations (throttling leads to decryption failures).

SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC08.name: Grant Revocation
SEC-KV-ENC-005-RC08.desc: Revoking the specific "Grant" that allowed the DB service to use the key.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC01.name: Default Configuration Deployment
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC01.desc: Redis ships with all commands enabled by default; production instances deployed using unchanged default redis.conf files without security hardening.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC02.name: Missing rename-command Directives
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC02.desc: The rename-command configuration parameter not applied in production.conf to rename or disable FLUSHALL to empty string, leaving destructive commands accessible.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC03.name: Lack of ACL (Access Control List) Implementation
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC03.desc: Organizations running Redis 6.0+ without configuring ACL rules (introduced in Redis 6.0) that would deny @admin command categories to non-admin users.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC04.name: Insufficient Change Management
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC04.desc: No formal process to review and lock database configurations; ad-hoc manual configuration changes allow developers or operators to omit security controls.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC05.name: Configuration Drift from Development
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC05.desc: Dev/staging environments often have loose security configurations (commands enabled for testing/debugging) copied directly to production without modification.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC06.name: Lack of Deployment Automation and Validation
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC06.desc: Manual deployment processes without automated scripts that enforce security baselines; no pre-deployment validation that dangerous commands are disabled.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC07.name: Replication and Sentinel Default Behavior
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC07.desc: Redis Sentinel and replication don't restrict command access by default; replicas inherit master's command accessibility from configuration files.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC08.name: Absence of Secret Management Integration
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC08.desc: No integration with HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, or equivalent to centrally manage and enforce immutable security configurations across all instances.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC09.name: Shared Configuration Templates
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC09.desc: Organizations use shared redis.conf templates across dev, staging, and production without environment-specific overrides for security controls.

SEC-KV-DATA-002-RC01.name: Encryption disabled or not configured
SEC-KV-DATA-002-RC01.desc: default unencrypted storage used without security configuration

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC10.name: Insufficient Operator Training
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC10.desc: Database operators and DevOps engineers unaware that FLUSHALL deletes all databases or lack understanding of rename-command syntax and ACL configuration requirements.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC11.name: Emergency Access Override Procedures
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC11.desc: Emergency maintenance procedures bypass normal security controls temporarily and are not rolled back after incident resolution.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC12.name: No Enforcement of Least Privilege
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC12.desc: Application connections use default user or root accounts with +@all permissions instead of restricted accounts with specific command allowlists.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC13.name: Lack of Audit Logging and Detection
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC13.desc: No monitoring for FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB commands; incidents go undetected until data loss is discovered.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC14.name: ElastiCache Parameter Group Misconfiguration
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC14.desc: AWS ElastiCache users create parameter groups without restricting dangerous commands; default groups may allow FLUSHALL depending on Redis version compatibility.

SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC15.name: Version Pinning Gaps
SEC-KV-CMD-001-RC15.desc: Older Redis versions (pre-6.0) lack ACL feature entirely; organizations unable to upgrade due to application compatibility continue using vulnerable configurations.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC01.name: Default Command Accessibility
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC01.desc: Redis enables CONFIG GET/SET/RESETSTAT/REWRITE by default; no security measure prevents privileged command execution in default configuration.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC02.name: Missing Command Disabling
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC02.desc: rename-command CONFIG "" not applied to disable CONFIG commands entirely; even rename-command CONFIG <secret> is insufficient if attacker discovers the renamed command.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC03.name: ACL Not Restricting @admin Commands
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC03.desc: Redis 6.0+ ACL system not configured to exclude @admin category from application user accounts; applications receive +@all or include +@admin in permissions.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC04.name: Overly Permissive Service Account Permissions
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC04.desc: Database service accounts (used by application code) created with administrative privileges rather than restricted to read/write operations only.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC05.name: No Validation of dir/dbfilename Parameters
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC05.desc: CONFIG SET allows changing `dir` (working directory) and `dbfilename` (RDB save path); no validation prevents writing RDB files to attacker-controlled or rootcausely-accessible paths.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC06.name: Insufficient Path Validation and Sandboxing
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC06.desc: Operating system permissions and chroot/container sandboxing not applied to restrict where Redis can write files; Redis runs with overly-permissive file system permissions.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC07.name: Configuration Hot-patching Without Audit
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC07.desc: CONFIG SET used to modify runtime settings (logfile, loglevel, timeout) without audit logging of who changed what and when.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC08.name: Lack of CONFIG Persistence Lock-down
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC08.desc: CONFIG REWRITE allows permanent modification of redis.conf file at runtime; attackers can modify on-disk config to persist malicious settings across restarts.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC09.name: Missing File System Integrity Monitoring
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC09.desc: Redis configuration files not monitored for unauthorized changes; modified redis.conf persists undetected across restarts.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC10.name: ElastiCache Parameter Group Full Access
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC10.desc: ElastiCache users allowed to modify parameter groups without restriction; parameter groups include CONFIG equivalents that can be modified at runtime.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC11.name: No Separation of Configuration Management Role
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC11.desc: Same personnel/service account that deploys applications also manages database configurations; no segregation of duties between deployment and database administration.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC12.name: Insufficient Monitoring of CONFIG Commands
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC12.desc: Command logging/auditing not enabled or reviewed; CONFIG SET commands executed by attackers go undetected until damage occurs.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC13.name: Cleartext Configuration Storage
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC13.desc: redis.conf files stored in version control or documentation systems without encryption; sensitive configuration details (requirepass, ACL users) exposed to developers.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC14.name: Lack of Configuration Validation at Startup
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC14.desc: Database startup scripts don't validate redis.conf parameters against security policy; startup completes successfully with insecure settings.

SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC15.name: Shared Configuration Across Environments
SEC-KV-CMD-002-RC15.desc: Single redis.conf used for development, staging, and production; development's permissive CONFIG settings copied to production.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC01.name: Default Configuration Includes @dangerous Category
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC01.desc: Redis DEBUG command category included in default command set with @dangerous tag, but disabled by ACL only if explicitly configured.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC02.name: No ACL Restricting @dangerous Category
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC02.desc: ACL rules not implemented to deny -@dangerous to non-admin users; all database clients receive default user permissions including DEBUG access.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC03.name: DEBUG Commands Used for Development
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC03.desc: DEBUG OBJECT, DEBUG SEGFAULT, DEBUG OOM used during development/testing; left enabled when code migrates to production without configuration review.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC04.name: Insufficient Pre-Production Security Testing
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC04.desc: Security configuration validation not included in deployment pipeline; configs deployed with DEBUG commands enabled because they pass functionality tests but fail security tests.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC05.name: Module Replacement Evasion
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC05.desc: Attackers load custom modules that override DEBUG command to return false information or hide malicious behavior; original DEBUG command replaced but detection tools still see it as available.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC06.name: DEBUG SEGFAULT Denial-of-Service
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC06.desc: DEBUG SEGFAULT triggers intentional segmentation fault, crashing Redis process; no rate-limiting or permission check prevents unauthenticated users from DoS-ing the service.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC07.name: DEBUG OOM Memory Exhaustion
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC07.desc: DEBUG OOM command fills memory with garbage data until out-of-memory kill occurs; enables memory exhaustion attacks without requiring large data injection.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC08.name: MONITOR Command Exposure
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC08.desc: MONITOR (related to DEBUG functionality) streams all commands processed by Redis, allowing attackers to observe all operations including credentials passed in commands.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC09.name: No Audit of Debug Command Execution
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC09.desc: Command logging not configured to detect DEBUG command execution; attacks go unnoticed until crash/data corruption discovered.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC10.name: Development/Test Cluster Reuse
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC10.desc: Development clusters with DEBUG enabled accidentally used as production clusters; no environmental separation enforces different security postures.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC11.name: Container Image Misconfiguration
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC11.desc: Docker/container images built with loose security configurations for development reused in production; image layer contains redis.conf enabling DEBUG commands.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC12.name: Insufficient Role-Based Access Control
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC12.desc: Monitoring/debugging roles given DEBUG access to troubleshoot issues but role not restricted when user transfers to non-debugging team.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC13.name: Emergency Maintenance Override
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC13.desc: Production incidents trigger temporary elevation of permissions to DEBUG level for troubleshooting; permissions not revoked after incident.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC14.name: HeadCrab Malware Pattern
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC14.desc: Attackers load modules that override DEBUG command definition; overridden DEBUG command used to hide malware activities and detect evasion.

SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC15.name: No Detection of DEBUG Overrides
SEC-KV-CMD-003-RC15.desc: Monitoring systems don't verify that DEBUG command points to original Redis code; replaced DEBUG commands allow malware to hide.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC01.name: O(N) Time Complexity Not Understood
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC01.desc: Developers unaware that KEYS command scans entire keyspace; assumes O(1) operation and calls it frequently from application code.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC02.name: No Alternative SCAN Command Implementation
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC02.desc: Application code uses KEYS instead of SCAN for key enumeration; developers either unaware of SCAN or prioritize simplicity over performance.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC03.name: ACL Not Restricting @dangerous Category
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC03.desc: KEYS categorized as @dangerous by Redis; ACL rules not configured to deny -@dangerous to application user accounts.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC04.name: Default User Has All Permissions
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC04.desc: Applications connect with default user or root account with +@all permissions; KEYS command accessible without restriction.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC05.name: No Application-Level Command Validation
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC05.desc: Application logic doesn't validate or restrict which commands are sent to Redis; any command in protocol is executed without client-side filtering.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC06.name: Absence of Rate Limiting on Commands
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC06.desc: KEYS command executed repeatedly without rate limiting; each invocation blocks server from processing other requests.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC07.name: Output Buffer Unlimited Growth (CVE-2025-21605)
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC07.desc: Redis default configuration imposes no limits on client output buffers; KEYS result sets large enough to exhaust memory.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC08.name: DoS Monitoring Gap
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC08.desc: No alerts for slow commands or long-running operations; KEYS command blocks server but goes undetected without explicit slow-command logging configured.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC09.name: Scan Migrations Never Completed
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC09.desc: Legacy code using KEYS never refactored to SCAN; accumulated technical debt leaves dangerous commands in production code paths.

SEC-KV-DATA-001-RC10.name: Pattern-based key generation without sanitization
SEC-KV-DATA-001-RC10.desc: PII fields included without hashing or encoding

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC10.name: Command Execution From Untrusted Sources
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC10.desc: Database credentials or connection strings available to third-party integrations or contractors; external systems execute KEYS for unauthorized data discovery.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC11.name: Lazy Debugging Practices
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC11.desc: Operations staff use KEYS for emergency troubleshooting instead of proper monitoring tools; ad-hoc KEYS commands from redis-cli during incidents.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC12.name: No Client-Side Command Filtering
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC12.desc: Application middleware/proxy layer not configured to intercept and reject KEYS commands; all commands pass through to Redis.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC13.name: Lack of Operational Dashboards
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC13.desc: No real-time visibility into command execution patterns; KEYS commands executed but not surfaced in dashboards.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC14.name: Memcached Stats Cachedump Equivalent
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC14.desc: Memcached stats cachedump command provides key enumeration similar to KEYS; causes same performance issues and goes unused/abused in production.

SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC15.name: Testing Only at Small Scale
SEC-KV-CMD-004-RC15.desc: Performance testing uses small datasets where KEYS completes quickly; production datasets large enough that KEYS execution causes visible degradation, but testing didn't reveal it.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC01.name: Lua Scripting Enabled by Default
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC01.desc: Redis enables EVAL/EVALSHA by default; Lua interpreter running in every Redis instance unless explicitly disabled.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC02.name: CVE-2025-49844 Lua Use-After-Free Vulnerability
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC02.desc: Critical vulnerability (CVSS 10.0) in Lua garbage collector allows authenticated users to escape sandbox and execute arbitrary native code; affects all Redis versions with Lua.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC03.name: Authentication Required But Often Missing
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC03.desc: Vulnerability requires authentication, but 60,000+ exposed Redis instances lack any authentication at all; attacker-controlled scripts executed with full Redis privileges.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC04.name: No ACL Restriction on EVAL/EVALSHA
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC04.desc: ACL rules not configured to deny -@dangerous or -@script commands; application and external users can execute arbitrary scripts.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC05.name: Lua Scripts Stored in Unencrypted Form
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC05.desc: SCRIPT LOAD caches scripts in memory without encryption; script source code accessible to attackers with read permissions or memory access.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC06.name: Dynamic Script Generation
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC06.desc: Applications generate Lua scripts dynamically based on user input; untrusted input incorporated into scripts leading to code injection.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC07.name: Script Injection via EVAL
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC07.desc: EVAL command accepts script source code as argument; scripts generated from untrusted sources (user input, external APIs) leading to arbitrary script execution.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC08.name: No Script Signature Verification
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC08.desc: Scripts loaded via EVALSHA don't verify that SHA1 corresponds to expected/safe script; attacker can load malicious script and force EVALSHA to execute it.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC09.name: Replication of Malicious Scripts
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC09.desc: EVAL scripts replicated to all cluster replicas; a single malicious script executed on master replicates to all replicas, spreading exploit.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC10.name: Script Persistence Across Restarts
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC10.desc: SCRIPT LOAD persists scripts in memory during instance lifetime; scripts may survive restart if AOF includes SCRIPT LOAD commands.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC11.name: Lua Sandbox Bypass Techniques
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC11.desc: Attackers develop new sandbox escape techniques; existing security controls become outdated as Lua framework evolves.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC12.name: No Command Interception for Malicious Patterns
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC12.desc: Application code doesn't validate scripts before executing; all EVAL requests pass through to Redis without inspection.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC13.name: Insufficient Monitoring of Script Execution
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC13.desc: SCRIPT LOAD and EVAL execution not logged/monitored; malicious scripts loaded undetected.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC14.name: Container/Cloud Environment Exploitation
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC14.desc: Exposed Redis instances in cloud environments execute scripts to compromise host; scripts access environment variables, SSH keys, container runtime APIs.

SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC15.name: Long-Running Scripts Consume Resources
SEC-KV-CMD-005-RC15.desc: SCRIPT FLUSH not called between requests; accumulated scripts consume memory; long-running scripts (intentional or malicious) block server.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC01.name: MODULE LOAD Command Unrestricted by Default
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC01.desc: Redis enables MODULE LOAD/UNLOAD/LIST by default; any authenticated user can load arbitrary compiled native modules.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC02.name: No ACL Restriction on MODULE Commands
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC02.desc: ACL rules not configured to deny -@admin (which includes MODULE commands); application and external users can load modules.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC03.name: Dynamic Module Loading Not Monitored
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC03.desc: MODULE LOAD commands executed without audit logging; attacker loads malicious module undetected.

SEC-KV-DATA-002-RC02.name: Performance optimization prioritization
SEC-KV-DATA-002-RC02.desc: developers choose speed over encryption despite security requirements

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC04.name: Modules Bypass Lua Sandbox Restrictions
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC04.desc: Custom modules can override Redis commands and expose internal APIs; modules can access raw memory, bypass permissions, and execute arbitrary native code.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC05.name: HeadCrab Malware Loader Pattern
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC05.desc: Real-world malware (HeadCrab) loads custom Redis modules for persistence and command override; modules replace legitimate commands (MODULE, CLIENT, DEBUG, CONFIG, SHUTDOWN, MONITOR, SLAVEOF, REPLICAOF) with stubs.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC06.name: Module Persistence in RDB/AOF
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC06.desc: Modules referenced in RDB snapshots or AOF logs; when Redis restarts, modules are automatically reloaded from persistence files.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC07.name: Malicious Module Override Detection Evasion
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC07.desc: Modules override default commands (especially monitoring/debugging commands) to hide their presence and the attacker's activities from detection tools.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC08.name: No Code Signing for Modules
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC08.desc: Modules loaded from untrusted sources (attacker-controlled URLs, compromised package repositories) without verification of publisher identity.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC09.name: Compiled Module Binary Inspection Difficulty
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC09.desc: Security teams cannot easily reverse-engineer or verify safety of pre-compiled .so/.dll module binaries; modules treated as black boxes.

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC10.name: Module Persistence Configuration
SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC10.desc: modules-ignore-max-memory setting and module caching allow modules to consume memory or persist settings outside normal database controls.

SEC-KV-DATA-001-RC09.name: Keys built from user-supplied input without validation
SEC-KV-DATA-001-RC09.desc: direct concatenation of form fields into keys

SEC-KV-CMD-006-RC11.name: RDB/AOF Injection via Module Configuration

SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC08.name: Alert escalation not configured
SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC08.desc: security events not escalated to appropriate teams

SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC09.name: Monitoring tool complexity
SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC09.desc: SIEM/monitoring platforms too complex to configure quickly

SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC10.name: Cost constraints
SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC10.desc: monitoring solutions cost-prohibitive for smaller organizations

SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC11.name: On-call rotation not alert-aware
SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC11.desc: alerts generated but no one assigned to respond

SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC12.name: Response procedures not defined
SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC12.desc: alerts generated but response workflows don't exist

SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC13.name: False negative blindness
SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC13.desc: focus on high-volume attacks misses subtle reconnaissance

SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC14.name: Third-party monitoring gaps
SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC14.desc: managed services don't alert on customer-side configurations

SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC15.name: Retention limits preventing analysis
SEC-KV-AUDIT-004-RC15.desc: monitoring data purged before analysis possible **Application-Level Root Causes:** - Applications don't implement database-level monitoring integration points - No application-layer correlation of database events with application logs - Monitoring focused on performance metrics rather than security events - Alert infrastructure not designed to distinguish legitimate from suspicious activity

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC07.name: Privilege Escalation Chain
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC07.desc: Attacker with limited MySQL privileges can read sensitive system files (/etc/passwd, application config files with credentials) to escalate access

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC12.name: Recursive query amplification
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC12.desc: Attackers craft queries that trigger internal recursive similarity searches; unprotected recursion depth causes stack overflow or infinite loops.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC13.name: Vector replication overhead in distributed systems
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC13.desc: Oversized vectors are replicated across cluster nodes; replication bandwidth is exhausted before indexing completes.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC14.name: Metadata field explosion alongside vectors
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC14.desc: Attackers insert vectors with thousands of metadata fields; metadata processing consumes more resources than vector storage.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC15.name: Insufficient isolation of resource consumption per tenant
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC15.desc: In multi-tenant deployments, one tenant's resource-exhausting queries starve other tenants' legitimate traffic.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC01.name: PostgreSQL ident authentication default
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC01.desc: PostgreSQL's default `pg_hba.conf` for remote connections (IPv4/IPv6) sometimes specifies `ident` authentication, delegating trust to the ident server or OS identification.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC02.name: Oracle REMOTE_OS_ROLES enabled
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC02.desc: Oracle's initialization parameter `REMOTE_OS_ROLES` set to TRUE allows OS groups to have database roles, enabling remote OS authentication for non-local connections.

SEC-SQL-ENC-003-RC08.name: Backup and Recovery Complexity
SEC-SQL-ENC-003-RC08.desc: Organizations do not understand that backups encrypted with TDE require the encryption key to restore, adding operational complexity for disaster recovery and off-site backup storage.

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC04.name: Kubernetes service exposure misconfiguration
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC04.desc: LoadBalancer service type with no network policies or service ingress restrictions; kubectl proxy exposed to 0.0.0.0; no NetworkPolicy CRDs defined for pod-to-pod communication

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC05.name: Docker/Docker Compose port mapping to 0.0.0.0
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC05.desc: Ports mapped as -p 0.0.0.0:6333:6333 instead of localhost:6333 or using internal networks; no bridge network isolation

SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC03.name: Microsoft deprecation lag
SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC03.desc: Microsoft marked extended stored procedures as deprecated in SQL Server 2005+ but did not remove them until later versions, creating a false sense of safety for prolonged use.

SEC-SQL-ACC-011-RC01.name: Open / in-flight transactions detected
SEC-SQL-ACC-011-RC01.desc: One or more sessions currently hold an open transaction. Each row identifies the session, login, host, program, target database, transaction start time, elapsed seconds, CPU and the SQL text so long-running, blocking or suspicious transactions can be triaged.

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC13.name: Insufficient Documentation
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC13.desc: DBA instructions or runbooks don't explicitly mention disabling local_infile; it's treated as a minor configuration detail

SEC-SQL-CFG-003-RC09.name: Documentation Failures
SEC-SQL-CFG-003-RC09.desc: Server documentation and asset inventory don't flag which databases are production vs. non-production; no single source of truth on what should exist

SEC-SQL-CFG-003-RC12.name: Automated Provisioning Templates
SEC-SQL-CFG-003-RC12.desc: Infrastructure-as-code or automated deployment scripts include sample database creation steps that persist through production deployments

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC06.name: Cloud provider security group defaults
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC06.desc: AWS security groups, Azure NSGs, or GCP firewall rules configured with inbound 0.0.0.0/0; cloud provider defaults often allow all traffic

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC12.name: Metadata Filters Bypassed via Type Coercion
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC12.desc: Metadata filter comparing `user_id == 123` (string vs. int); JavaScript-style coercion allows `"123xyz"` to match expected value

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC12.name: Replication without encryption between nodes
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC12.desc: Distributed vector DBs replicate data between cluster nodes; internal replication traffic may be unencrypted if TLS is not enabled.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC02.name: Insufficient input validation on embedding dimensions
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC02.desc: Systems accept vectors of any dimensionality; attackers insert vectors with wrong dimensions that corrupt indexing structures.

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC14.name: Insufficient encryption key protection
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC14.desc: Encryption keys stored in configuration files, environment variables, or unencrypted key vaults are compromised if file/memory access is obtained.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC13.name: Temporal metadata leakage via timestamps
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC13.desc: Creation/modification timestamps in metadata combined with content can enable inference of sensitive activity patterns or user behavior.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC03.name: Semantic crafting of malicious vectors for retrieval
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC03.desc: Attackers carefully craft vector values such that they are semantically similar to common queries, ensuring high retrieval probability.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC14.name: Batch metadata export without filtering
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC14.desc: Bulk export, migration, or replication operations dump all metadata without selective redaction or encryption.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC15.name: Insufficient classification/tagging of PII fields
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC15.desc: Teams don't classify which metadata fields contain PII; all fields are treated equally, leading to over-exposure.

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC15.name: Full-text logging of vectors in debug/audit logs
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC15.desc: Debug or audit logs capture unencrypted vector payloads for troubleshooting; these logs are often stored with lower security than production data.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC04.name: No authenticity verification of ingested documents
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC04.desc: RAG systems ingest from web sources, APIs, or user uploads without verifying document integrity or source authenticity.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC01.name: Cleartext storage of identifiers
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC01.desc: Metadata fields store user IDs, email addresses, or names in plaintext alongside vectors without encryption.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC05.name: Metadata injection via unsanitized filters
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC05.desc: Applications build metadata filters from user input without proper escaping; attackers inject conditions to retrieve restricted metadata.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC05.name: Automatic ingestion from compromised or untrusted sources
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC05.desc: Systems automatically crawl web content, GitHub repositories, or rootcause databases; attackers publish poisoned content expecting ingestion.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC02.name: Insufficient input validation during metadata ingestion
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC02.desc: Applications concatenate user-supplied data directly into metadata without sanitization; PII is embedded unintentionally.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC01.name: Adversarial document injection with hidden instructions
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC01.desc: Attackers craft documents containing embedded prompts (e.g., "IGNORE ALL PRIOR INSTRUCTIONS") that, when embedded and retrieved, are passed to the LLM as trusted context.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC02.name: Semantic similarity guarantees retrieval of poisoned content
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC02.desc: An attacker embeds a document with carefully chosen text that remains semantically similar to legitimate queries, ensuring retrieval by the RAG system.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC15.name: Batch embedding exposure without sanitization
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC15.desc: Bulk export or backup features that dump embeddings without aggregation or filtering expose entire datasets to inversion attacks.

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC02.name: Performance optimization prioritized over encryption
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC02.desc: Vector database vendors optimize for low-latency similarity search; encryption at rest adds computational overhead that conflicts with performance SLAs.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC03.name: Metadata exposed in query results
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC03.desc: Vector database queries return metadata alongside embeddings to provide context; this metadata is logged, cached, or transmitted unencrypted.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC03.name: LLM implicit trust of retrieved context
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC03.desc: Large language models inherently treat retrieved context as authoritative and factual; they don't distinguish between user input and retrieved documents.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC04.name: No content validation before embedding
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC04.desc: Vector DBs accept any content without checking for embedded prompts, instructions, or adversarial payloads.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC04.name: Over-permissive metadata exposure in RAG retrieval
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC04.desc: RAG systems return full metadata records (including PII) to LLMs as context, which may then repeat sensitive information in generated outputs.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC05.name: Insufficient separation of concerns between context and system prompt
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC05.desc: RAG systems concatenate retrieved context directly into the LLM prompt without clear demarcation; the LLM cannot distinguish adversarial instructions.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC02.name: Credentials in client-side code
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC02.desc: API keys exposed in frontend JavaScript, React, or web client code where they are visible in network requests or browser developer tools.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC03.name: Accidental commits to version control
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC03.desc: API keys committed to rootcause GitHub, GitLab, or other repositories. Automated scanners continuously scan repositories for leaked credentials.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC04.name: Credentials in .env files tracked in Git
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC04.desc: `.env` files containing API keys accidentally committed to version control systems instead of being listed in `.gitignore`.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC05.name: API keys logged in application logs
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC05.desc: Secrets exposed in console.log(), debug statements, or logging libraries that send logs to third-party services.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC06.name: Process memory and core dumps
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC06.desc: API keys visible in process memory dumps, crash reports, or system monitoring tools that capture environment variables.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC07.name: Credentials in deployment artifacts
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC07.desc: API keys baked into Docker images, container registries, or CI/CD pipeline logs.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC14.name: Multi-tenant isolation not configured
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC14.desc: Databases accessible by any tenant without namespace or shard-level isolation enforcement.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC08.name: Shared credentials across environments
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC08.desc: Single API key used for development, staging, and production, increasing exposure surface and blast radius.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC09.name: API keys in API documentation or Postman collections
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC09.desc: Credentials embedded in API documentation, Postman collections, or shared development resources.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC10.name: Credentials in error messages and stack traces
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC10.desc: API keys revealed when exceptions occur and full error details are returned to clients or logged.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC11.name: Credentials in configuration management systems
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC11.desc: Secrets stored unencrypted in Ansible, Terraform, Kubernetes manifests, or other infrastructure-as-code without proper secret vaults.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC12.name: API keys in browser history and Slack messages
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC12.desc: Credentials pasted in chat messages, tickets, emails, or browser autocomplete history.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC13.name: Weak API key generation
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC13.desc: Predictable or short API keys that can be brute-forced or guessed by attackers.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC07.name: Unauthenticated anonymous access
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC07.desc: Services configured to allow anonymous/unauthenticated access, especially during development that moves to production.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC14.name: No credential rotation policy
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC14.desc: API keys never rotated, meaning compromised keys remain valid indefinitely.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC15.name: Inadequate access controls on key storage
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC15.desc: Shared cloud storage, GitHub gists, or shared drives containing API keys with no access restrictions.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC16.name: Credentials in application backups and snapshots
SEC-VEC-AUTH-001-RC16.desc: API keys present in database dumps, VM snapshots, or backup files stored without encryption.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC01.name: Authentication disabled by default
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC01.desc: Vector databases ship with authentication entirely disabled, requiring explicit enablement that users often skip.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC02.name: Hardcoded default admin accounts
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC02.desc: Databases distributed with pre-configured default user/password combinations (e.g., admin/admin, root/root) that remain unchanged.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC03.name: Default credentials in documentation
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC03.desc: Installation guides and quick-start tutorials showing default credentials that developers copy without changing them.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC04.name: No password set for privileged accounts
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC04.desc: Root or admin users created without requiring a password during installation or first run.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC08.name: Service accounts without credentials
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC08.desc: Shared service accounts or API clients using placeholder or example credentials.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC12.name: Lack of prompt template escaping in RAG
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC12.desc: When retrieved documents are inserted into prompt templates, there is no escaping to prevent injection (similar to SQL injection).

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC09.name: Development credentials in production
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC09.desc: Test/demo credentials like "test123" or "demo" never changed when deploying to production.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC12.name: Chroma authentication provider not configured
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC12.desc: CHROMA_SERVER_AUTHN_PROVIDER and CHROMA_SERVER_AUTHN_CREDENTIALS_FILE environment variables not set.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC06.name: JSON/structured metadata without encryption
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC06.desc: Metadata stored as JSON documents or structured fields with no field-level encryption exposes all fields equally.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC15.name: Default certificate configurations
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC15.desc: Self-signed or example certificates used in production without proper validation or pinning.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC16.name: Minimal access controls on first deployment
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC16.desc: Role-based access controls (RBAC) not configured, all users treated as administrators.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC17.name: Initial setup wizard completed with defaults
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC17.desc: Installation tools with interactive setup skipped or run with all defaults accepted.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC02.name: Self-signed certificates not accepted by clients
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC02.desc: Clients configured to reject self-signed certificates, leading developers to disable certificate verification entirely.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC03.name: Certificate validation disabled
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC03.desc: Application code or client libraries configured with `verify=false`, `insecure=true`, or equivalent flags to bypass TLS validation.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC04.name: Development-to-production copy without TLS updates
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC04.desc: Configuration copied from development (HTTP) environment to production without enabling TLS.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC12.name: Insufficient access controls on vector data
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC12.desc: Unencrypted, unauthenticated vector access (e.g., via misconfigured S3 buckets, exposed endpoints) enables direct download of embedding datasets for offline inversion research.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC05.name: TLS certificate not installed or configured
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC05.desc: Server certificates, private keys, or CA certificates missing, not copied to correct paths, or incorrectly referenced in configuration.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC06.name: Expired TLS certificates
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC06.desc: Certificates expired but not renewed; certificate renewal automation missing or failed.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC07.name: Self-signed certificate used without client-side pinning
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC07.desc: Custom TLS setup without implementing certificate pinning to validate certificate authenticity.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC08.name: TLS disabled for "performance"
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC08.desc: Network overhead concerns lead to TLS being disabled, especially in internal network deployments.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC10.name: Data plane traffic unencrypted
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC10.desc: Client-to-server traffic uses HTTP instead of HTTPS; separate encryption not implemented at application level.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC13.name: Temporal inversion via embedding history
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC13.desc: Storing versioned embeddings over time enables attackers to observe how embeddings change, revealing underlying source data evolution and enabling differential reconstruction.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC14.name: Semantic similarity guarantees aid inversion
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC14.desc: The core property of vector DBs (semantic similarity) is exactly what enables inversion: crafted query vectors can recover semantically similar original documents.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC12.name: Replication traffic in plaintext
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC12.desc: Database replication from master to replica configured without TLS, exposing data in transit.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC14.name: No TLS for inter-service communication
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC14.desc: Microservice network calls between application and vector database, or between vector database components, unencrypted.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC15.name: TLS handshake validation disabled
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC15.desc: Application configured to skip hostname verification or SNI validation in TLS handshakes.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC06.name: Ingestion from untrusted sources without sanitization
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC06.desc: RAG systems automatically ingest content from web sources, forums, or user-submitted documents; malicious actors seed these sources with injected prompts.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC07.name: No anomaly detection on retrieved context
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC07.desc: Systems don't monitor whether retrieved documents contain unusual instruction-like patterns or metadata flags indicating poisoning.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC16.name: Downgrade attacks possible
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC16.desc: Server and client negotiate to older, insecure TLS versions (TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1) due to permissive version configuration.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC17.name: Certificate chain validation incomplete
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC17.desc: Intermediate CA certificates not installed, breaking full certificate chain validation.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC18.name: mTLS (mutual TLS) not enforced
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC18.desc: Client certificates required at server but not validated; server certificates not pinned at client.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC19.name: Logging/monitoring traffic in plaintext
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC19.desc: Vector database metrics, logs, or monitoring data exported without encryption over HTTP.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC20.name: Load balancer TLS offloading without backend encryption
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC20.desc: TLS terminated at load balancer but traffic to backend database unencrypted.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC08.name: Query parameter manipulation via metadata filters
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC08.desc: Attackers craft queries with specific metadata filters designed to retrieve poisoned documents, bypassing content-based filtering.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC09.name: Indirect injection via retrieval chain poisoning
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC09.desc: An attacker poisons intermediate retrieval steps (e.g., tool outputs or intermediate context); each step retrieves poisoned context for the next.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC13.name: Multiple round-trip retrieval enabling amplification
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC13.desc: Iterative RAG architectures (where model output triggers further retrievals) enable attackers to amplify injected instructions across multiple rounds.

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC02.name: Weak Namespace Isolation Logic
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC02.desc: Database engine relies on application-layer namespace filtering rather than enforcing strict boundaries at the query engine level, creating bypass opportunities

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC03.name: Missing or Disabled Data Plane Authentication
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC03.desc: Authentication enforced on control plane (admin APIs) but disabled on data plane operations (query/upsert), allowing direct namespace traversal

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC04.name: Implicit Resource Access Without Explicit Grants
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC04.desc: RBAC not configured to require explicit permission per namespace/collection; default behavior grants access to all unspecified resources

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC05.name: JWT/Token Claims Unauthenticated Against Resource
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC05.desc: Token validation succeeds but doesn't verify claims (e.g., tenant_id) match the requested namespace; claim-to-resource mapping skipped

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC06.name: Multi-Level Isolation Failure (Logical + Physical)
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC06.desc: Logical isolation at query layer fails (namespaces enumerable without permission) combined with physical storage not truly isolated

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC07.name: Shared Data Structure with Misconfigured Access Control
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC07.desc: Single shard/partition serves multiple tenants but ACLs or RLS policies contain misconfiguration or boolean logic errors in access rules

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC04.name: Unencrypted backup and snapshot procedures
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC04.desc: Scheduled snapshots or backups of vector indices are written to storage (S3, NAS, local disk) without encryption, leaving sensitive data exposed.

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC08.name: API Key Scoped to Project Level Instead of Namespace
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC08.desc: API key created with project-level permissions rather than namespace-level, allowing key holder to query any namespace within that project scope

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC09.name: Cross-Tenant Cache Collision
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC09.desc: Query results cached at system level without tenant_id in cache key; one tenant's cached result returned to another due to cache key collision

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC04.name: Credentials Reused Across Multiple Services/Environments
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC04.desc: Single API key shared between read-only analytics and write-enabled ingestion; both inherit full permissions of parent key

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC10.name: Metadata-Based Tenant Confusion
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC10.desc: System trusts embedded tenant_id in vector metadata rather than enforcing tenant context server-side; malicious metadata allows cross-querying

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC11.name: Unvalidated Tenant Context in Application Middleware
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC11.desc: Application sets tenant context via HTTP headers without validating against authenticated user's actual tenant affiliation

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC12.name: Partition Key Omitted in Query Filters
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC12.desc: Query layer accepts queries without partition key even though partition scheme exists; queries return results across partitions

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC05.name: Insufficient access controls on storage backend
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC05.desc: Vector data stored on underlying infrastructure (NAS, object storage, SSD) relies on OS-level permissions that may be misconfigured or inherited from overly-permissive defaults.

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC13.name: Administrative Override Without Audit Trail
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC13.desc: Admin/super-user API key used in production queries; super-user bypass of tenant isolation not logged or detected

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC05.name: Temporary Elevated Permissions Never Revoked
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC05.desc: Key created with elevated permissions for one-time maintenance; elevated permissions not downscaled after task completion

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC14.name: Race Condition During Namespace Initialization
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC14.desc: Namespace created with default permissive ACL; window exists before RLS/RBAC policies applied where all tenants have access

SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC15.name: Connection Pool Tenant Context Reuse
SEC-VEC-ACC-001-RC15.desc: Shared database connection pool reuses connections; tenant context set in one request not cleared before next request, causing cross-tenant leakage

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC02.name: Overly Broad Permission Templates
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC02.desc: Vendor-provided roles (e.g., "Editor", "Developer") include more permissions than necessary; no granular permission selection available

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC03.name: No Automated Permission Audit Process
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC03.desc: Keys created and deployed without subsequent auditing; no scheduled review to detect and revoke over-scoped keys

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC11.name: Unencrypted temporary files during indexing
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC11.desc: Vector index construction processes create temporary files (intermediate states, sorting buffers) that are not encrypted during the indexing pipeline.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC10.name: Insufficient model instruction override barriers
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC10.desc: LLM system prompts lack robust mechanisms to prevent override; embedded instructions like "RESPOND AS:" successfully change model behavior.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC11.name: Embedding model retention of instruction syntax
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC11.desc: Embedding models preserve enough semantic information about prompt-like text that instructions embedded in documents survive the embedding process.

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC06.name: Complex Permission UI Causing Misconfiguration
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC06.desc: Permission assignment GUI/CLI confusing; operators select broad category instead of specific operations (e.g., "all" instead of individual actions)

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC07.name: Default Permissions in Infrastructure-as-Code Templates
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC07.desc: Terraform/CloudFormation templates ship with permissive defaults; values not updated before production deployment

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC08.name: No Distinction Between API Key Types
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC08.desc: Single API key type issued; no concept of read-only vs. read-write vs. admin keys; all keys inherit full capability set

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC09.name: Inheritance of Parent Resource Permissions
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC09.desc: User/role granted broad permissions at project level; all child resources automatically inherit those permissions without restriction

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC06.name: Elasticsearch index data not encrypted natively
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC06.desc: Elasticsearch does not encrypt index data at rest; field-level encryption via plugins is optional and rarely enabled.

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC10.name: Service Accounts Granted User-Level Admin Permissions
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC10.desc: Microservices configured with API key having user-level admin permissions instead of narrower service account permissions

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC11.name: API Key Not Scoped to Specific Collections/Indexes
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC11.desc: Full create/delete permissions across all collections; no method to restrict key to specific collection or read-only mode on specific collection

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC12.name: Documentation Showing Overly Permissive Examples
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC12.desc: Official docs/tutorials use `"permissions": "*"` or equivalent; developers copy-paste without reading scoping options

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC13.name: Coarse Permission System Without Granularity
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC13.desc: Vendor API only offers coarse permission grants (read, write, delete, admin) with no ability to split read from write or delete from create

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC14.name: Permission System Incompatible with Least Privilege
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC14.desc: Boolean role model (is_admin: true/false) instead of granular ACL; can't express "read-only on collection X and read-write on collection Y"

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC15.name: Missing Resource-Level Permission Validation in SDK
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC15.desc: SDK doesn't validate that key has required permissions before execution; error only returned after failed API call

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC09.name: Metadata stored alongside unencrypted vectors
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC09.desc: Vector databases store metadata (IDs, field names, filter values) in plaintext next to embeddings, exposing context even if vectors alone were encrypted.

SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC16.name: Secret Manager Integration Not Enforcing Scope
SEC-VEC-ACC-002-RC16.desc: Secrets stored in Vault/AWS Secrets Manager but scope/permissions not encoded or validated by secret manager on retrieval

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC18.name: Expression Language Injection
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC18.desc: If metadata used in SpEL (Spring Expression Language), OGNL, or similar, attacker injects expressions like `${7*7}` or `#{...}`

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC14.name: Metadata-based injection via retrieved field values
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC14.desc: Attackers poison metadata fields (titles, descriptions, tags) with instructions; these are returned and processed by the LLM.

SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC15.name: Cross-tenant retrieval poisoning in multi-tenant RAG
SEC-VEC-ATK-001-RC15.desc: In shared environments, an attacker poisons documents in a shared index accessible to other tenants, causing mass injection.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC01.name: Unrestricted write access to vector index
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC01.desc: Vector databases allow anonymous or unauthenticated inserts; attackers add malicious vectors without credentials.

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC01.name: Unvalidated Metadata Stored Without Sanitization
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC01.desc: User-supplied metadata accepted as-is; no input validation, encoding, or sanitization before persistence

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC02.name: Metadata Rendered in UI Without HTML Encoding
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC02.desc: Metadata displayed in dashboard/UI without HTML entity encoding; `<script>` tags and event handlers execute in browser context (persistent XSS)

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC03.name: Metadata Concatenated Into Filter Queries
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC03.desc: Metadata fields concatenated directly into filter/search queries without parameterization; attacker injects query operators or SQL syntax

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC04.name: No Type Checking on Metadata Fields
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC04.desc: Metadata accepted as arbitrary JSON; if field expected to be string, integer/object injection causes type confusion in query builder

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC05.name: Server-Side Template Injection via Metadata
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC05.desc: Metadata rendered in server-side templates without escaping; template expressions injected via metadata values

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC10.name: Key management infrastructure not implemented
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC10.desc: Even when encryption is enabled, lack of key rotation, secure key storage, or key access controls renders encryption ineffective.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC09.name: Insufficient access controls on metadata filtering
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC09.desc: Metadata filtering queries have weak authorization; users can filter by sensitive fields they shouldn't access.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC10.name: PII embedded in vector ID strings
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC10.desc: Vector IDs (used for deduplication and retrieval) contain business logic encoding sensitive data (e.g., "user_12345_SSN_789").

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC06.name: LIKE/Regex Operator Misuse in Metadata Filters
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC06.desc: Metadata filters using LIKE or regex operators; attacker injects regex metacharacters to bypass intended filter logic

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC07.name: Sensitive Metadata Exposed in Error Messages
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC07.desc: Internal metadata (IDs, system information) exposed in error responses; attacker uses leaked information to craft injection payloads

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC08.name: No Schema Validation for Metadata Structure
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC08.desc: Metadata accepted as free-form key-value pairs; no JSON schema or type definition enforcing expected structure

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC10.name: Metadata Field Names Processed as Code
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC10.desc: If metadata keys construct database field names, attacker injects keys like `__proto__` causing prototype pollution (JavaScript) or similar attacks

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC11.name: Log Injection via Metadata
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC11.desc: Metadata logged without escaping; attacker injects log format strings or newlines to forge log entries or exfiltrate data

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC07.name: Metadata stored in multiple places without consistent redaction
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC07.desc: PII appears in metadata, logs, backups, and caches; redaction is inconsistent across these surfaces.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC11.name: Metadata exposure in error messages
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC11.desc: Error responses from vector queries include metadata snippets that reveal structure, field names, or sample PII values.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC12.name: Unencrypted metadata in transit
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC12.desc: Metadata sent over HTTP/unencrypted protocols is intercepted or logged by proxies, firewalls, or network monitoring tools.

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC13.name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in Metadata
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC13.desc: If metadata format supports XML or API accepts XML metadata elements, XXE payloads embedded in metadata

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC14.name: CSV/TSV Injection in Metadata Export
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC14.desc: Metadata exported to CSV and used in spreadsheets; injected formula like `=cmd|'/c calc'!A0` executed when file opened in Excel

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC15.name: Path Traversal via Metadata
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC15.desc: If metadata constructs file paths for export/storage, attacker injects `../` sequences to write to arbitrary paths

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC16.name: Command Injection via Metadata in Post-Processing
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC16.desc: Metadata passed to external scripts/tools without escaping; OS command injection via backticks or shell metacharacters

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC17.name: LDAP Injection via Metadata
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC17.desc: If metadata used in LDAP queries for access control, attacker injects LDAP filter syntax to modify queries

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC19.name: No Content-Type/MIME Type Validation
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC19.desc: Metadata field accepts arbitrary content-type; attacker uploads JavaScript blob labeled as image, later served with wrong MIME type causing XSS

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC20.name: Metadata Used in Unormalized Cache Keys
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC20.desc: Metadata used directly in cache key; attacker injects cache poisoning payload via metadata, returns malicious cached result to other users

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC01.name: Insufficient embedding model entropy
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC01.desc: Embedding models trained on limited datasets or with weak randomization produce lower-dimensional representations that retain more information about original inputs, enabling efficient reconstruction attacks.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC02.name: Access to multiple query results enabling statistical inference
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC02.desc: Attackers querying similar inputs and observing embedding differences can triangulate original data characteristics through differential analysis and proximity patterns.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC03.name: Model architecture weaknesses
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC03.desc: Embedding models designed primarily for semantic similarity rather than privacy preserve too much dimensional information about input structure, allowing gradient-based or optimization-based inversion attacks.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC04.name: No differential privacy mechanisms applied pre-embedding
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC04.desc: Absence of noise injection (Laplacian or Gaussian) during embedding generation leaves deterministic mappings vulnerable to exact or approximate reconstruction.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC05.name: rootcausely known embedding model specifications
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC05.desc: Widely-used embedding models (sentence-transformers, OpenAI embeddings) are reverse-engineerable; attackers can probe them locally and apply learned attack patterns to target vectors.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC06.name: Membership inference via centroid proximity
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC06.desc: Storing aggregate centroids or cluster centers along with individual vectors enables attackers to infer if specific data points were in training sets based on distance metrics.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC07.name: Attribute inference through embedding clustering
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC07.desc: High-dimensional clustering analysis can reveal correlated attributes (e.g., salary ranges, healthcare conditions) without reconstructing full records, leaking sensitive characteristics.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC08.name: Query access logs revealing input patterns
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC08.desc: Unencrypted query logs showing repeated queries for similar embeddings enable attackers to correlate patterns and refine inversion attacks iteratively.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC09.name: Insufficient dimension reduction
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC09.desc: Embeddings stored at full dimensionality without compression retain structural information vulnerable to dimensionality reduction attacks or PCA-based reconstruction.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC10.name: Model output gradients exposed via API responses
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC10.desc: Some vector DB APIs return confidence scores or similarity gradients; attackers use these in gradient-based inversion attacks to reconstruct original text.

SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC11.name: Cross-dataset embedding analysis
SEC-VEC-DAT-001-RC11.desc: Attackers comparing embeddings across multiple databases (internal vs. rootcause sources) can identify and reconstruct private training data by finding matching embeddings.

SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC08.name: Collection/namespace names reveal sensitive information
SEC-VEC-DAT-003-RC08.desc: Collection names like "medical_records_cancer_treatment" or "financial_clients_high_net_worth" leak classification and PII via database introspection.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC06.name: Centroid drift via targeted vector insertion
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC06.desc: By inserting vectors with specific values, attackers shift cluster centroids in k-means indexing, causing legitimate queries to return wrong results.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC07.name: Index structure manipulation through adversarial insertions
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC07.desc: Attackers insert vectors that degrade index performance or cause balanced tree structures to become unbalanced, affecting retrieval.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC08.name: Metadata injection to alter filtering and retrieval
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC08.desc: Attackers inject vectors with misleading metadata that causes filtering rules to retrieve wrong or biased results.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC09.name: Bulk data poisoning via compromised ETL pipelines
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC09.desc: Attackers compromise upstream data sources (databases, APIs, data lakes); poisoned data flows into vector DBs during scheduled ingestion.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC10.name: Supply chain attack via rootcause datasets
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC10.desc: Attackers poison rootcause datasets (Wikipedia, GitHub, Common Crawl) knowing that enterprise RAG systems will ingest them.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC11.name: User-submitted content poisoning in collaborative systems
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC11.desc: RAG systems accepting user-submitted documents or fine-tuning data; users intentionally or maliciously submit poisoned content.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC12.name: Insufficient deduplication allowing repetitive poisoning
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC12.desc: Systems lack deduplication mechanisms; attackers insert the same malicious vector multiple times, increasing its influence on retrieval.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC13.name: No consistency checks on ingested vectors
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC13.desc: Systems don't validate that ingested vectors are actually outputs of the claimed embedding model (enabling fake/crafted vectors).

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC14.name: Temporal persistence of poisoned vectors
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC14.desc: Poisoned vectors remain in the index indefinitely; no automatic quarantine, flagging, or review process identifies and removes them.

SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC15.name: Distributed poisoning across multiple tenants/indices
SEC-VEC-ATK-002-RC15.desc: In large-scale deployments, attackers systematically poison vectors across multiple organizational units or customer namespaces.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC02.name: Memory exhaustion from oversized embeddings
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC02.desc: Attackers send massive dimension vectors (e.g., 1 million dimensions instead of expected 768) consuming gigabytes of memory per request.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC03.name: No per-request or per-user resource limits
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC03.desc: Rate limiting and quota systems focus on request count, not computational cost; memory/CPU intensive requests bypass protections.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC04.name: Buffer overflow in dimension-dependent allocation
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC04.desc: Indexing structures allocate buffers based on vector dimension without bounds checking; oversized dimensions cause heap overflows.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC05.name: Malformed vector format causing parsing DoS
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC05.desc: Attackers submit vectors with incorrect format (null bytes, non-numeric characters, truncated data) causing parsers to crash or consume excessive resources.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC06.name: Sparse vector processing inefficiencies
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC06.desc: Vector DBs supporting sparse vectors don't validate that dimension indices are within reasonable ranges; huge index values cause memory exhaustion.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC07.name: Query payload size without bounds checking
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC07.desc: Batch query requests with thousands of vectors aren't throttled; attackers submit huge payloads exhausting network and memory resources.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC08.name: Inefficient index structure traversal on edge cases
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC08.desc: Query processing algorithms degrade to O(n) or worse on certain vector patterns; attackers craft vectors triggering worst-case complexity.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC09.name: No timeout on similarity computations
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC09.desc: Vector similarity search (especially brute-force on large indices) runs indefinitely without timeouts; attackers trigger searches over billions of vectors.

SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC10.name: Connection state exhaustion via incomplete requests
SEC-VEC-ATK-003-RC10.desc: Attackers open connections, send partial vector data, and leave connections open; the database holds state, exhausting available connections.

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC07.name: Reverse proxy/load balancer misconfigured
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC07.desc: Nginx, HAProxy, or cloud load balancer exposing database port directly instead of restricting to internal IP ranges or VPCs

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC08.name: NAT/port forwarding bypassing internal restrictions
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC08.desc: Router or firewall port forwarding rules exposing internal database ports; VPN/tunnel allowing rootcause access

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC09.name: SSH/bastion host port exposure
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC09.desc: SSH port to database host exposed; attackers use SSH to access internal database services

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC10.name: Container registry or CI/CD pipeline leaking access details
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC10.desc: Database endpoints hardcoded in rootcause container images or GitHub repositories with exposed endpoints

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC11.name: DNS resolution to rootcause IP
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC11.desc: DNS A records pointing to rootcause IPs instead of private route 53/internal DNS; subdomain enumeration reveals database endpoints

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC12.name: Terraform/Infrastructure-as-Code default values
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC12.desc: IaC templates (Terraform, CloudFormation) using 0.0.0.0/0 as default CIDR; copy-paste errors from rootcause documentation

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC13.name: Firewall rules disabled or misconfigured
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC13.desc: Host-based firewalls (ufw, firewalld) disabled; iptables rules removed; Windows Defender firewall rules bypassed

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC14.name: Development/test environments not secured
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC14.desc: Production-like databases spun up in development with default open networking; staging environments left accessible after testing

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC15.name: API gateway or application server proxying without authentication
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC15.desc: Backend API server proxies requests to database without API key/auth checks; clients directly call database through API gateway discovery

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC02.name: Certificate validation disabled at application layer
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC02.desc: curl with -k (--insecure); Python urllib3 with assert_hostname=False; Java with disabled hostname verification

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC03.name: Self-signed certificates not imported to trust store
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC03.desc: Client applications reject self-signed certs because root CA not in system trust store or application's trust bundle; CA certificate not provided to SDK

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC04.name: Missing certificate pinning
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC04.desc: Applications accept any valid certificate from any CA rather than pinning to specific certificate hash or rootcause key; no cert pinning implementation in client libraries

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC06.name: Downgrade attacks from HTTPS to HTTP
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC06.desc: Server supports both HTTP and HTTPS; client code accidentally uses HTTP endpoint; lack of HSTS headers allows SSLStrip attacks

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC07.name: Expired or revoked certificates not checked
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC07.desc: Certificate validation skips expiration checks; OCSP stapling not implemented; CRL checking disabled; client library not verifying Certificate Revocation Lists

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC09.name: Certificate transparency bypass
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC09.desc: Fake certificates issued without logging to CT logs; client doesn't verify CT logs; attacker uses compromised CA to issue fraudulent certificates

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC10.name: DNS spoofing/poisoning
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC10.desc: Client resolves database FQDN to attacker IP; DNS queries intercepted and redirected; DNS over HTTPS (DoH) not used; internal DNS not secured

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC11.name: ARP spoofing on local network
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC11.desc: Attacker performs ARP spoofing to intercept traffic between client and database; gratuitous ARP packets redirect traffic to attacker system

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC12.name: Proxy or middleware man-in-the-middle
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC12.desc: Corporate proxy or transparent proxy performing HTTPS interception with self-signed certificates; client forced to accept proxy's cert; HTTP interception proxies between app and database

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC13.name: CA certificate compromise
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC13.desc: Attacker compromises CA and issues fraudulent certificates; fake CA cert added to system trust store; rogue CA roots in trust store

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC14.name: Client-side certificate validation logic flaws
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC14.desc: Custom certificate validation code with bugs; hostname verification bypassed; wildcard certificate misused; SAN validation incorrect

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC15.name: No mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC15.desc: Only server certificate validated; client certificate not required; attacker impersonates legitimate client after intercepting traffic; no bi-directional authentication

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC02.name: No application-layer logging implemented
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC02.desc: Application code does not log query execution; middleware layer doesn't capture request/response; no audit proxy between app and database

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC04.name: Elasticsearch audit logging not configured
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC04.desc: Elasticsearch requires X-Pack license and manual audit logging configuration; audit logging disabled by default; audit log categories not enabled; audit.index not configured

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC05.name: OpenSearch audit logging not enabled
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC05.desc: Audit logging not activated in OpenSearch configuration; audit-action not set; security plugin disabled; immutable audit logs not configured

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC07.name: No query aggregation to centralized logging
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC07.desc: CloudWatch/Stackdriver/DataDog not configured to receive logs; ELK stack not deployed; Splunk or logging service not collecting database logs

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC08.name: Log retention policy not configured
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC08.desc: Logs deleted after default TTL (e.g., 7 days); log files rotated and purged; no log archive to S3/GCS; audit trail cannot be reconstructed

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC13.name: Application layer does not correlate users with queries
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC13.desc: No middleware capturing user context; database user/app service not logging queries with user ID; multi-tenant systems not tracking per-tenant queries

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC14.name: Chroma relies on external logging
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC14.desc: Chroma server logs HTTP requests but no built-in audit trail; no query tracking without implementing custom middleware; request logging must be configured at proxy/container level

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC12.name: Milvus proxy doesn't expose detailed query metadata
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC12.desc: Queries logged at network level but embedding vectors not captured; query parameters not logged; user identity not tied to queries

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC15.name: Compliance logging framework not implemented
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC15.desc: No structured logging for regulatory requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, PCI-DSS); no separate immutable audit log storage; no tamper-proof log mechanism

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC01.name: Raw query vectors logged in plaintext
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC01.desc: Vector embeddings (float arrays) logged as part of query requests; query_vector=[0.123, 0.456, ...] captured in logs; embedding content exposed for reconstruction

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC02.name: Search terms not redacted from logs
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC02.desc: Natural language query terms logged: "find documents about patient X" or "search for contract with ABC Corp"; sensitive keywords visible in plaintext logs

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC03.name: Metadata exposed in query logs
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC03.desc: Associated metadata (user IDs, document IDs, collection names) logged alongside queries; tenant identifiers revealing multi-tenant data access patterns; result metadata (similarity scores, result IDs) logged

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC04.name: API request/response logging without sanitization
