SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC04.desc: Full HTTP body logged including query parameters and search filters; response payloads containing document identifiers and similarity scores; headers containing API keys logged

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC05.name: Application logs not masking sensitive data
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC05.desc: Application middleware logging full query objects; SDKs logging query parameters; debug logging capturing all request/response data

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC06.name: Query parameters containing secrets
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC06.desc: API keys, bearer tokens passed in query parameters instead of headers and logged; database credentials in connection strings logged; personally identifiable information (PII) in filters

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC07.name: Logs stored unencrypted at rest
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC07.desc: Log files on disk unencrypted; CloudWatch logs, Stackdriver, or logging service not using encryption; log backups and archives stored in plaintext; S3 buckets with logs not using server-side encryption

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC08.name: Logs transmitted unencrypted in transit
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC08.desc: Log forwarding over HTTP instead of HTTPS; syslog without TLS; log aggregation services accessed over unencrypted connections; log shipping not using TLS

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC09.name: Log access controls not implemented
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC09.desc: Logs accessible to all users/services without authentication; log storage has permissive file permissions (644 or 666); cloud log buckets rootcausely readable or unintentionally shared

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC10.name: Verbose logging in production
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC10.desc: Debug logging enabled in production deployments; LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG or similar causing detailed output; stack traces with variable values logged

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC11.name: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch storing full query DSL
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC11.desc: Elasticsearch audit logging may capture full query DSL including filters and parameters; sensitive query structures exposed; JSON queries logged as-is

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC14.name: Version control systems logging queries
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC14.desc: Database query templates committed to git with example data; test logs with real vectors checked into repository; CI/CD pipeline logs capturing query examples

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC15.name: Monitoring/observability tools capturing full payloads
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC15.desc: Prometheus capturing full metric labels with sensitive data; Jaeger or APM tools tracing full request/response bodies; network packet capture tools recording query content

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC12.name: pgvector logs containing SQL statements
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC12.desc: PostgreSQL log_statement=all capturing full SQL with WHERE clauses containing sensitive data; pg_audit capturing sensitive search conditions; log_min_duration_statement revealing slow queries with parameters

SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC08.name: Multi-vendor environment complexity
SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC08.desc: Organizations running multiple database platforms lack a unified hardening framework, causing inconsistency in which defaults are addressed.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC03.name: OS service account access
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC03.desc: Applications run as OS service accounts (e.g., the database service account), and the database trusts that OS identity for authentication, bypassing password checks.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC02.name: Outdated extensions with known vulnerabilities
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC02.desc: Failure to regularly update extensions exposes databases to rootcausely known CVEs, including privilege escalation flaws like CVE-2022-2625

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC08.name: No Cipher Suite Hardening Standard
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC08.desc: There is no organizational standard for which cipher suites should be enabled. Each database is configured differently, and older configurations include weak suites.

SEC-SQL-AUD-001-RC02.name: Missing audit plugin/extension
SEC-SQL-AUD-001-RC02.desc: The required database audit plugin or extension is not installed or loaded into the server's shared memory.

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC09.name: RSA Key Exchange Still Enabled
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC09.desc: Configurations allow RSA-based key exchange, which is vulnerable to decryption if the private key is compromised. TLS 1.2+ should prefer ECDHE for forward secrecy, but RSA is still enabled.

SEC-SQL-ENC-003-RC01.name: Not Aware of TDE Feature
SEC-SQL-ENC-003-RC01.desc: Database administrators are unaware that TDE exists in their database version or believe TDE is only available in premium/enterprise editions and assume they cannot use it.

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC02.name: Third-Party Vendor Requirements
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC02.desc: Vendor-supplied software or legacy integrations explicitly require the OS command execution interface to be enabled for functionality; vendors refuse to support configurations without it.

SEC-SQL-PRI-003-RC02.name: Database meets High-level criteria but configured as Basic/Medium
SEC-SQL-PRI-003-RC02.desc: Database holds sensitive data of >100k subjects or >10 authorised users, which triggers High-level requirements. If classified lower, controls are likely insufficient.

SEC-SQL-PRI-003-RC03.name: External access enabled without High-level controls
SEC-SQL-PRI-003-RC03.desc: Mixed-mode auth + remote access enabled but encryption / audit / strong auth not configured to High-level standard.

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC04.name: Inadequate Change Control
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC04.desc: OS command execution is enabled during development/testing and never disabled when promoting to production due to missing security review in change control process.

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC05.name: SQL Injection Vulnerability
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC05.desc: Applications with SQL injection vulnerabilities allow attackers to enable OS command execution if it is available; attacker gains operating system access through the database.

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC11.name: Weaviate lacks granular query logging
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC11.desc: GraphQL logs not enabled by default; REST API request logging minimal; module execution not logged; vector search operations not captured in audit trail

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC07.name: Lack of Monitoring and Auditing
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC07.desc: Absence of query logging or auditing means attackers can enable and use OS command execution without detection or alerting.

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC08.name: Knowledge Gap on Alternatives
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC08.desc: DBAs unaware of secure alternatives (external process invocation, ETL tools, external procedures) default to OS command execution for system integration tasks.

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC09.name: Privilege Escalation via Weak Credentials
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC09.desc: Compromised low-privilege database login can use OS command execution to pivot to operating system administrator access if the database service account is overprivileged.

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC10.name: Lateral Movement Capability
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC10.desc: Once attacker gains OS command execution access, they can use operating system commands to execute lateral movement tools for network reconnaissance and further compromise.

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC11.name: Persistence Mechanisms
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC11.desc: OS command execution allows creation of scheduled tasks, registry/cron modifications, or service installation for maintaining post-exploitation persistence.

SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC12.name: Backup Restoration from Compromised Environments
SEC-SQL-CFG-001-RC12.desc: Production databases restored from backups created in compromised lower-level environments may retain OS command execution enabled configuration.

SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC02.name: Backward compatibility requirements
SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC02.desc: Multi-customer or long-running systems cannot easily drop support for OS command execution or other extended procedures without breaking dependent applications.

SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC05.name: High barrier to refactoring
SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC05.desc: Migrating from OS command execution to alternatives requires database code changes, application code changes, infrastructure changes, and regression testing across all environments.

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC06.name: Unvalidated User Input
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC06.desc: If application accepts filename or path from users/queries without validation, attackers can exploit local_infile to read arbitrary system files

SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC08.name: Missing monitoring and enforcement
SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC08.desc: No detection mechanisms, audit policies, or triggers prevent unauthorized use or re-enabling of OS command execution after it has been disabled.

SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC10.name: Security compliance misalignment
SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC10.desc: Compliance policies may require disabling OS command execution, but the control itself is ineffective because administrators with sufficient privileges can re-enable it at will.

SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC13.name: Redis storing commands in memory/logs
SEC-VEC-LOG-002-RC13.desc: MONITOR command capturing all Redis commands including search parameters; redis-cli history logging search queries; command logging exposing vector data access patterns

SEC-SQL-ENC-004-RC12.name: No Centralized Key Management Service
SEC-SQL-ENC-004-RC12.desc: The organization lacks a centralized key management system (KMS), making it difficult to issue, store, and manage encryption keys for backups. Encryption is not implemented due to this operational gap.

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC07.name: Cipher Suite Configuration Not Updated
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC07.desc: Database cipher suite configuration inherits weak defaults from OS-level TLS/SSL libraries. Even though stronger ciphers exist, the organization has not explicitly configured the database to prefer them.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC05.name: OS authentication module delegation
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC05.desc: Database configured to delegate authentication to an OS-level module (PAM, SSPI, or similar), including for remote connections where OS identity cannot be reliably verified.

SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC01.name: Default trust-based local authentication
SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC01.desc: Database installation creates default authentication rules that allow unauthenticated local or loopback connections, and these permissive defaults are left unchanged in production.

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC02.name: Legitimate Data Loading Requirements
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC02.desc: Applications genuinely require LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE for bulk data imports (ETL processes, initial data seeding); feature left enabled after deployment

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC03.name: Inadequate Server-Side Controls
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC03.desc: Focus on enabling the feature during development for testing but no implementation of compensating controls (file restrictions, rate limiting) before production use

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC04.name: Unclear Default Behavior
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC04.desc: Documentation confusion about whether local_infile is enabled by default; DBAs/developers assume it's secure by default when it's not

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC09.name: Legacy Unix ident server
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC09.desc: Database configured to use the legacy ident protocol (port 113) for network authentication, which provides no cryptographic verification of client identity.

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC08.name: Information Disclosure
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC08.desc: Enabled local_infile allows reading database configuration files, application source code, or other server files that contain secrets or architectural information

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC09.name: Implicit Trust Model
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC09.desc: Configuration assumes all clients connecting to the database are trusted; local_infile enabled system-wide rather than per-session or per-user

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC11.name: Backup Retention
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC11.desc: local_infile enabled during initial bulk loading and never disabled; remains active through multiple backup/restore cycles and environment promotions

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC12.name: Third-Party Application Defaults
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC12.desc: Vendor-supplied applications (analytics tools, middleware) set local_infile=ON in their deployment templates without organization-specific review

SEC-SQL-CFG-005-RC03.name: Undocumented Historical Change
SEC-SQL-CFG-005-RC03.desc: Trace flag enabled during system migration or upgrade; change documentation lost or DBA who made change departed organization

SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC13.name: Knowledge loss and staff turnover
SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC13.desc: Original architects and developers who implemented OS command execution functionality have left; current teams lack documentation on why it was enabled and what depends on it.

SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC15.name: Absence of Host-Based Firewalls
SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC15.desc: Database server running without local firewall rules restricting inbound connections. Relies solely on network-layer controls.

SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC16.name: Infrastructure Drift from Code
SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC16.desc: Database manually configured with rootcause access outside of IaC processes. Actual deployed configuration differs from what security reviews approved.

SEC-SQL-NET-003-RC01.name: Default Allow Firewall Posture
SEC-SQL-NET-003-RC01.desc: Operating system and network firewalls ship with default-allow outbound policies. Outbound traffic is rarely restricted unless explicitly configured as default-deny.

SEC-SQL-NET-003-RC02.name: Egress Filtering Not Implemented
SEC-SQL-NET-003-RC02.desc: Organizations focus resources on inbound protection (perimeter security) while neglecting outbound traffic controls. Egress filtering is less common and more complex than ingress.

SEC-SQL-NET-003-RC10.name: DNS Unrestricted Outbound Access
SEC-SQL-NET-003-RC10.desc: Database servers with unrestricted DNS resolution capability to external servers, enabling initial reconnaissance and command-and-control communication.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC01.name: Incomplete asset discovery and inventory
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC01.desc: Organizations lack comprehensive visibility into which database servers exist, their exact versions, and their current patch levels, making it impossible to patch systems they don't know exist.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC06.name: Insufficient supply chain verification
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC06.desc: No cryptographic signing or integrity checking of extensions allows compromised or malicious extensions to be installed from untrusted sources

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC07.name: Inadequate extension inventory management
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC07.desc: Organizations lack comprehensive lists of installed extensions, versions, and their security postures, making vulnerability assessment impossible

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC08.name: Extensions granted excessive privileges by default
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC08.desc: Many extensions create functions with SECURITY DEFINER or similar high-privilege attributes that remain even when not needed

SEC-SQL-PRI-001-RC08.name: Third-Party Integration Limitations
SEC-SQL-PRI-001-RC08.desc: Off-the-shelf software or ORMs (Object-Relational Mappers) used by the organization may not support native database encryption functions, forcing clear text storage to ensure compatibility.

SEC-SQL-PRI-002-RC08.name: Client-Side "Debug" Modes
SEC-SQL-PRI-002-RC08.desc: Drivers (JDBC/ODBC) or ORMs (Hibernate/Entity Framework) are configured to output generated SQL to standard output/files. These logs are often ingested by centralized logging tools (Splunk/ELK) alongside system logs.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC09.name: Lack of runtime sandboxing
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC09.desc: Untrusted languages execute without proper isolation, allowing direct filesystem access, network operations, and process execution

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC08.name: No regular password audits
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC08.desc: Organizations fail to use default password audit tools or scanning utilities to identify accounts with default or weak passwords

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC12.name: Extensions not included in patch management
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC12.desc: Extension updates are often overlooked during database patching cycles, leaving security fixes unapplied

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC14.name: Inadequate logging of extension-related activities
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC14.desc: CREATE EXTENSION, ALTER EXTENSION, and extension function executions often lack proper audit trails

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC01.name: Failure to change default passwords during installation
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC01.desc: Database administrators neglect to modify well-known default passwords immediately after database creation, leaving systems vulnerable to trivial attacks

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC05.name: Default accounts not properly locked
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC05.desc: Accounts like CTXSYS, MDSYS, and DBSNMP remain unlocked after installation, contrary to security best practices

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC11.name: Default accounts granted DBA privileges
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC11.desc: Many default accounts like DBSNMP and CTXSYS have powerful system privileges that can be exploited if compromised

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC02.name: Databases upgraded from legacy versions preserving insecure defaults
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC02.desc: Upgrades from older database versions preserve unlocked default accounts or weak security settings that were created before the vendor improved installation security.

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC04.name: Lack of automated password policy enforcement
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC04.desc: The default password policy profile lacks complexity requirements, allowing weak passwords to persist indefinitely.

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC06.name: Inadequate password verification functions
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC06.desc: Failure to enable or customize password verification functions allows simple, guessable passwords that match usernames or follow predictable patterns.

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC09.name: Insufficient account lifecycle management
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC09.desc: Default accounts created during database feature or component installation are not tracked, reviewed, or properly configured with strong credentials.

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC10.name: Weak password hashing in older versions
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC10.desc: Legacy database versions use weak password hashing algorithms that can be cracked offline, making default or simple passwords especially dangerous.

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC13.name: Oracle's historical practice of creating numerous default accounts
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC13.desc: Each Oracle component and option creates its own accounts, expanding the attack surface with hundreds of potential entry points

SEC-DOC-INJ-005-RC15.name: Over-permissive API design
SEC-DOC-INJ-005-RC15.desc: Exposing full regex capabilities to untrusted users **Application-Level Root Causes:** - **Search and filter endpoints**: Accepting regex patterns in search boxes without validation - **MongoDB driver usage**: Using `$regex` operator with user input directly from request parameters - **Email/username validation**: Custom regex validation accepting user-supplied patterns - **MongoDB BSON library**: Historical ReDoS in js-bson module affecting MongoDB packages

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC02.name: IP access list not configured
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC02.desc: Cloud or self-hosted database instances not configured with an IP allowlist, leaving the service accessible from any network address instead of restricting to known client ranges.

SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC03.name: VPC endpoint/PrivateLink features not utilized
SEC-VEC-NET-001-RC03.desc: Private network endpoints or VPC peering not activated for the database service, forcing internet exposure as the sole access path instead of using private connectivity.

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC05.name: TLS not enabled on server
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC05.desc: Database deployed with TLS disabled or not configured, allowing client connections and data transfer over unencrypted channels.

SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC08.name: Weak TLS versions (< 1.2) configured
SEC-VEC-NET-002-RC08.desc: Database configured to accept deprecated TLS versions (SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1) or weak cipher suites, allowing protocol downgrade attacks and weakened encryption.

SEC-DOC-DAT-004-RC02.name: Missing TTL (Time-To-Live) indexes
SEC-DOC-DAT-004-RC02.desc: TTL (Time-To-Live) expiration not configured for automatic deletion of aged documents, allowing data to persist beyond required retention periods.

SEC-SQL-VS-001-RC04.name: Conflict resolution favors server privileges
SEC-SQL-VS-001-RC04.desc: Vertica's architecture resolves privilege conflicts by allowing server-level privileges to supersede MC restrictions, creating unexpected escalation paths

SEC-DOC-AUTHZ-002-RC02.name: Authentication Disabled Entirely
SEC-DOC-AUTHZ-002-RC02.desc: Document database configured to allow unauthenticated connections; authentication never enabled after installation, resulting in no authorization system at all.

SEC-SQL-NET-002-RC09.name: Infrastructure as Code Using Defaults
SEC-SQL-NET-002-RC09.desc: Terraform and CloudFormation templates use default port values without parameterization for environment-specific alternatives.

SEC-DOC-DAT-002-RC08.name: Missing data security platform
SEC-DOC-DAT-002-RC08.desc: No dedicated data security platform or tooling deployed for sensitive data discovery, masking, or access monitoring.

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC01.name: Default Client Library Compilation
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC01.desc: MySQL client library compiled with ENABLED_LOCAL_INFILE=1 at build time; this default persists unless explicitly changed during compilation

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC01.name: Encryption disabled by default in most platforms
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC01.desc: Vector databases ship with encryption in transit but not at rest by default, requiring explicit configuration that many teams skip during deployment.

SEC-DOC-DAT-003-RC15.name: Development environment backups
SEC-DOC-DAT-003-RC15.desc: Test/staging backups not encrypted despite containing production-like data. Backup scripts not including encryption flags, managed service backup encryption not enabled, and CI/CD pipeline backup jobs not configured with encryption parameters.

SEC-DOC-AUD-001-RC02.name: Edition Limitations
SEC-DOC-AUD-001-RC02.desc: The organization is using the community (free) edition of the database, which often lacks enterprise auditing features such as detailed access logging and compliance reporting.

SEC-DOC-AUTH-005-RC11.name: Exposed authentication endpoints on default ports
SEC-DOC-AUTH-005-RC11.desc: Database authentication endpoints exposed on well-known default ports, easily discovered in network scans and targeted by automated attack tools.

SEC-DOC-AUTH-007-RC14.name: Incorrect X.509 subject format for database user
SEC-DOC-AUTH-007-RC14.desc: X.509 certificate-based authentication requires specific Distinguished Name (DN) format matching the database user identity; a mismatch causes authentication failure.

SEC-DOC-DAT-002-RC15.name: Insufficient security testing
SEC-DOC-DAT-002-RC15.desc: Access controls not tested for data exposure. Application-level causes include returning full documents without projection to hide sensitive fields, REST API endpoints exposing complete profiles without masking, GraphQL over-fetching returning unmasked nested data, and admin panels displaying unmasked customer data.

SEC-DOC-DAT-004-RC15.name: Conflicting legal requirements
SEC-DOC-DAT-004-RC15.desc: Tax/legal obligations vs. privacy right to deletion creating retention confusion. Application-level causes include TTL expiration not configured on timestamp fields for automatic document deletion, batch deletion scripts causing performance issues leading to deferred deletions, and archive-then-delete workflows where data is moved to archive but never deleted from the primary database.

SEC-DOC-INJ-003-RC09.name: Access to database objects from JavaScript context
SEC-DOC-INJ-003-RC09.desc: Older MongoDB versions allowing `db` object access from `$where`

SEC-DOC-INJ-003-RC15.name: Third-party code vulnerabilities
SEC-DOC-INJ-003-RC15.desc: Dependencies using `$where` without developer knowledge **Application-Level Root Causes:** - **NodeGoat and similar vulnerable examples**: Direct concatenation of user input into `$where` expressions without validation - **Aggregation pipeline misuse**: Using `$function` or `$accumulator` operators with user-controlled code - **Custom validation logic**: Implementing complex validation in `$where` instead of application layer - **Spring Data MongoDB**: SpEL injection in `@Query` and `@Aggregation` annotations with `$where` expressions (CVE-2022-22980)

SEC-DOC-INJ-004-RC15.name: Default vulnerable configurations
SEC-DOC-INJ-004-RC15.desc: Framework defaults allowing object injection in authentication routes **Application-Level Root Causes:** - **Express/Node.js**: Using `req.body.username` and `req.body.password` directly in `User.findOne()` without sanitization - **PHP authentication**: Accepting `$_POST` arrays directly into MongoDB queries enabling `$ne` injection - **Passport.js misconfiguration**: Custom authentication strategies not validating input types - **JWT token generation**: Tokens generated based on injectable query results allowing privilege escalation

SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC05.name: Application Workaround Necessity
SEC-SQL-CFG-002-RC05.desc: Applications using MySQL Shell utilities (util.importTable, util.loadDump) require local_infile to be ON; feature left enabled after operations complete

SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC04.name: Lack of modern alternatives awareness
SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC04.desc: Developers and DBAs may not know about SQL Server Agent jobs, PowerShell integration, CLR integration, or other safer mechanisms for system tasks; xp_cmdshell remains the "known" approach.

SEC-SQL-PRI-002-RC10.name: Vertica Data Collector
SEC-SQL-PRI-002-RC10.desc: The `dc_requests_issued` table (and associated logs) retains the request string. If `save_query_text` is enabled (default), historical queries with PII literals are persisted on disk.

SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC09.name: NoSQL Injection via Metadata Operators
SEC-VEC-ACC-003-RC09.desc: Metadata filter expressions containing injection operators (e.g., NoSQL-style query operators) bypass access controls when user-supplied metadata is not sanitized before query construction.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC05.name: Trust authentication method enabled
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC05.desc: Database configured with a trust or no-authentication mode, allowing any local or network connection without credentials.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC06.name: Peer/ident authentication without password fallback
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC06.desc: PostgreSQL configured with peer/ident authentication for OS-level users, bypassing password requirements.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC10.name: Redis AUTH requirement disabled
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC10.desc: `requirepass` directive not set or commented out, allowing unrestricted access to Redis instances.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC11.name: Milvus authentication flag not enabled
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC11.desc: `common.security.authorizationEnabled` remains false, allowing all requests without authentication.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC13.name: Qdrant running without API key
SEC-VEC-AUTH-002-RC13.desc: `QDRANT__SERVICE__API_KEY` environment variable not set, allowing unauthenticated requests.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC09.name: Node-to-node traffic unencrypted
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC09.desc: Cluster communication between nodes configured without mutual TLS, allowing potential eavesdropping or tampering on internal replication and coordination traffic.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC11.name: Management API accessible over HTTP
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC11.desc: Database management API or administrative endpoints accessible over unencrypted HTTP instead of requiring HTTPS, exposing credentials and configuration data in transit.

SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC13.name: TCP port exposed instead of TLS port
SEC-VEC-AUTH-003-RC13.desc: Service listening on unencrypted port instead of TLS-enabled port due to misconfiguration, exposing data and credentials in transit.

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC03.name: Lack of Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) in open-source databases
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC03.desc: Open-source vector databases do not provide native Transparent Data Encryption (TDE); users must implement disk-level or application-level encryption separately.

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC07.name: Redis VSS data stored in-memory without disk encryption
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC07.desc: Redis VSS uses in-memory storage; unless the host system has full disk encryption, data is exposed if memory is dumped or swapped to disk.

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC08.name: PostgreSQL pgvector without host-level or TDE encryption
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC08.desc: pgvector embeddings inherit PostgreSQL row-level storage; without pgcrypto extension or host-level encryption, vectors are stored in plaintext in PostgreSQL's data files.

SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC13.name: Unencrypted query result caches
SEC-VEC-DAT-002-RC13.desc: Query result caching layers store unencrypted embeddings and search results for performance; cached data is exposed if storage or memory is compromised.

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC01.name: Logging disabled by default in vector DB
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC01.desc: Vector databases do not enable query-level logging by default, requiring explicit configuration to capture search requests for audit and compliance purposes.

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC03.name: pgaudit extension not installed/enabled
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC03.desc: PostgreSQL pgvector instances missing pgaudit extension; cloudsql.enable_pgaudit not set to "on"; pgaudit.log parameter not configured for READ/WRITE/ALL

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC06.name: MongoDB Atlas Query Logs not collected
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC06.desc: Profiler level not set (default 0 means logging disabled); Database Profiler not enabling slow query logging; log levels set to INFO instead of DEBUG for query capture

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC09.name: Redis default configuration has no query logging
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC09.desc: Redis INFO command returns limited stats; monitoring port (port 6379) doesn't log commands by default; DEBUG LOG not enabled; Redis Slow Log threshold too high

SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC10.name: Qdrant does not provide query-level audit logs
SEC-VEC-LOG-001-RC10.desc: Qdrant API does not log individual search requests; container logs may contain some HTTP activity but no query semantics; api-key authentication provides no audit trail of who searched

SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC12.name: Database Version Limitations
SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC12.desc: Older database versions do not support disabling TLS 1.0/1.1 at the database level and require OS-level configuration.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC08.name: No validation of OS identity
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC08.desc: Systems accepting OS usernames from clients over the network without cryptographic verification of actual OS user identity.

SEC-SQL-ENC-004-RC04.name: Backup Software License Limitations
SEC-SQL-ENC-004-RC04.desc: Encryption may be a premium feature in the backup tool, and the organization operates on a lower license tier that excludes encryption.

SEC-SQL-PRI-004-RC01.name: TDE / database-level encryption not enabled
SEC-SQL-PRI-004-RC01.desc: Database holds personal data but transparent data encryption (TDE) or equivalent database-level encryption is not enabled.

SEC-SQL-PRI-004-RC02.name: Sensitive columns stored without column-level encryption
SEC-SQL-PRI-004-RC02.desc: Columns identified as PII/sensitive are stored as plain types without Always Encrypted / TDE column / pgcrypto / equivalent.

SEC-SQL-PRI-004-RC03.name: Connections not enforced over TLS
SEC-SQL-PRI-004-RC03.desc: Server allows unencrypted connections; personal data in transit may traverse the network in plain text. Reg §9 requires encryption of data in transit when accessed remotely.

SEC-SQL-PRI-005-RC01.name: No audit specification configured
SEC-SQL-PRI-005-RC01.desc: Database engine has no audit specification, so no events are being recorded — Reg §6 requires logging access to personal data.

SEC-SQL-PRI-005-RC02.name: Audit configured but does not cover SELECT on PII tables
SEC-SQL-PRI-005-RC02.desc: An audit exists but does not include SELECT actions on tables holding personal data. Read access is the most common exposure path.

SEC-SQL-PRI-005-RC03.name: Audit log retention < 24 months
SEC-SQL-PRI-005-RC03.desc: Audit log files retained for less than 24 months, the minimum required by Reg §6 for High-level databases.

SEC-SQL-PRI-006-RC02.name: Application accounts hold sysadmin / db_owner
SEC-SQL-PRI-006-RC02.desc: Accounts whose name suggests an application or service have sysadmin / db_owner / equivalent — violates least privilege.

SEC-SQL-PRI-006-RC03.name: Stale logins retain access to personal data
SEC-SQL-PRI-006-RC03.desc: Logins with no recorded login activity for > 90 days still hold permissions on PII tables.

SEC-SQL-PRI-007-RC01.name: SQL logins without password policy
SEC-SQL-PRI-007-RC01.desc: SQL logins exist with check_policy=OFF / no password complexity, allowing weak passwords on accounts that may access personal data.

SEC-SQL-PRI-007-RC02.name: Shared / generic logins in use
SEC-SQL-PRI-007-RC02.desc: Logins with generic names (admin, app, svc, dba, root) are active and have access to personal data, defeating identity attribution required by Reg §6.

SEC-SQL-PRI-007-RC03.name: SA / superuser login enabled and active
SEC-SQL-PRI-007-RC03.desc: The instance's built-in superuser (sa / sys / postgres / root) is enabled and has been used recently — violates Reg §6 identity-verification requirements.

SEC-SQL-PRI-008-RC01.name: No recent backup of database holding personal data
SEC-SQL-PRI-008-RC01.desc: No full / differential backup recorded in the last 7 days. Reg §15 requires regular backups of personal data.

SEC-SQL-PRI-011-RC01.name: Teudat Zehut (Israeli national ID) columns unencrypted
SEC-SQL-PRI-011-RC01.desc: Columns matching teudat_zehut / tz / national_id / id_number patterns hold what is likely Israeli national IDs, stored without encryption.

SEC-SQL-PRI-011-RC02.name: Medical / health-data columns without classification
SEC-SQL-PRI-011-RC02.desc: Columns matching medical / diagnosis / health / treatment / prescription patterns hold sensitive medical data per PPL §7.

SEC-SQL-PRI-011-RC03.name: Religion / political-opinion / sexual-orientation columns exposed
SEC-SQL-PRI-011-RC03.desc: Columns matching religion / dat / political / orientation patterns hold sensitive opinion / belief / orientation data per PPL §7.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC04.name: Superuser privileges required for extension installation
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC04.desc: The CREATE EXTENSION command often requires superuser, forcing organizations to grant excessive privileges to users who only need specific extension functionality

SEC-SQL-PRI-001-RC15.name: Sensitive columns in cached plans / active transactions (PII)
SEC-SQL-PRI-001-RC15.desc: Detects PII data exposure via two SQL Server DMV sources: (a) cached query plans in sys.dm_exec_query_stats — broader historical view of queries that have executed against sensitive tables, retained while the plan stays in cache; (b) currently-uncommitted transactions in sys.dm_tran_active_transactions — sessions holding locks or state on PII data. Each row links a query/transaction to the specific sensitive column it references, including execution count, average CPU/IO, transaction state, and full SQL text.

SEC-SQL-AUD-015-RC01.name: Recent schema changes or DML detected via SQL Server Audit
SEC-SQL-AUD-015-RC01.desc: Returns every schema-change (CREATE/ALTER/DROP) and DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE) event recorded by the target database's audit subsystem over the last 24 hours. Auto-provisions audit infrastructure on first run for each vendor.

SEC-SQL-AUD-008-RC05.name: Cross-schema transactions outside application scope
SEC-SQL-AUD-008-RC05.desc: A session joins or accesses tables from two or more schemas that the associated application has no business reason to combine, suggesting unauthorized data correlation.

SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC01.name: Tautology patterns detected in active query text
SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC01.desc: Active queries contain always-true conditions such as OR 1=1, OR 'a'='a', or OR 1>0 that are characteristic of classic SQL injection payloads used to bypass WHERE-clause filtering.

SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC02.name: Stacked or chained query execution detected
SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC02.desc: A single query string contains multiple statement terminators followed by additional SQL commands, indicating a stacked-query injection where the attacker appends arbitrary statements to a legitimate request.

SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC03.name: UNION-based probing across unknown tables
SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC03.desc: Queries contain UNION SELECT constructs referencing system catalog tables or column counts inconsistent with the legitimate application, indicating UNION-based injection used to extract schema or data.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC01.name: Unknown login executing queries
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC01.desc: A login name not in the expected baseline is actively running transactions. This may indicate a newly created unauthorized account, a compromised credential, or a misconfigured application.

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC15.name: Default passwords in configuration files
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC15.desc: Database configuration tools, installation scripts, and vendor documentation often reference default passwords, embedding them in operational processes and making them widely known.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC02.name: Unexpected program or application connected
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC02.desc: Transactions are being executed by a program/application name not in the expected baseline. This may indicate unauthorized tooling, SQL injection via a web app, or direct database access bypassing application controls.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC03.name: Query activity on unexpected database
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC03.desc: Transactions target a database not in the expected baseline. This may indicate lateral movement, data exfiltration attempts, or misconfigured applications accessing the wrong database.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC04.name: Suspicious query patterns detected
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC04.desc: Running transactions contain suspicious SQL patterns such as bulk data extraction, schema discovery, privilege escalation attempts, or data modification from unexpected sources.

SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC04.name: Time-delay injection functions detected in active queries
SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC04.desc: Queries contain time-delay calls such as pg_sleep, WAITFOR DELAY, SLEEP(), or DBMS_LOCK.SLEEP, which are the hallmark of blind time-based SQL injection used to infer data without visible output.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC05.name: Sensitive data (PII) accessed in active transactions
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC05.desc: Active transactions are querying columns identified as containing sensitive/PII data (names, emails, SSN, credit cards, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth). First identifies PII columns via schema inspection, then checks if any running transaction references those columns or tables.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC11.name: Developers installing extensions without security review
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC11.desc: Database developers have authority to install extensions in development environments that later propagate to production without security assessment

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC13.name: Malicious extension objects can persist through backups
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC13.desc: Trojan objects created by compromised extensions survive database dumps and restores, maintaining backdoor access

SEC-SQL-ENC-003-RC16.name: Wallets and Key Storage Issues
SEC-SQL-ENC-003-RC16.desc: TDE encryption keys or key storage files are kept on the same server as the database, defeating the security purpose. Organizations disable TDE because proper external key management is too complex to implement.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC15.name: Trusted extension mechanism bypasses security controls
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC15.desc: The "trusted" flag allows non-superusers to install extensions that can still contain vulnerable or malicious code

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC03.name: Applications dependent on default credentials
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC03.desc: Third-party or legacy applications hardcode default passwords for accounts like DBSNMP, preventing administrators from changing them without breaking functionality

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC07.name: Fear of breaking database features by changing default passwords
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC07.desc: Administrators hesitate to change default passwords for service accounts used by management tools, built-in components, or internal features due to concerns about service disruption.

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC12.name: Lack of integration with enterprise password management
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC12.desc: Database passwords managed separately from corporate password vaults or identity providers, leading to inconsistent security controls and credential sprawl.

SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC14.name: Inadequate documentation of required default accounts
SEC-SQL-VS-003-RC14.desc: DBAs lack clear guidance on which default accounts are necessary versus which can be safely locked, leading to conservative approaches that leave accounts open

SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC05.name: Comment-based obfuscation or encoding in query text
SEC-SQL-AUD-009-RC05.desc: Queries contain inline SQL comments (/**/, --), hex-encoded strings, CHAR() concatenation, or URL-encoded characters used to obfuscate injection payloads and bypass input validation or WAF rules.

SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC01.name: Excessive information_schema or catalog enumeration
SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC01.desc: A single session issues an unusually high number of queries against information_schema, pg_catalog, sys.objects, or DBA_ views within a short window, consistent with automated schema mapping.

SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC02.name: System principal and user enumeration by non-admin account
SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC02.desc: A non-administrative account queries pg_roles, sys.server_principals, mysql.user, DBA_USERS, or equivalent views listing all database accounts, indicating attacker reconnaissance of the privilege landscape.

SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC03.name: Mass table and column listing within a single session
SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC03.desc: A session queries information_schema.columns or equivalent for all tables in a database in rapid succession, typically indicating an automated tool mapping the full column inventory for targeted exfiltration.

SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC04.name: Stored procedure and function source code enumeration
SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC04.desc: A non-DBA account retrieves the source definitions of stored procedures, functions, or packages from pg_proc, sys.sql_modules, information_schema.routines, or ALL_SOURCE, suggesting reconnaissance of business logic.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC06.name: SQL injection patterns in active transactions
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC06.desc: Active transactions contain classic SQL injection signatures such as tautology attacks (OR 1=1), UNION-based injection, stacked queries with semicolons, comment-based truncation, time-based blind injection (WAITFOR/SLEEP/BENCHMARK), and error-based extraction attempts.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC08.name: Privilege escalation attempts in transactions
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC08.desc: Non-admin users are executing DDL or DCL statements (CREATE, ALTER, DROP, GRANT, REVOKE, DENY) that modify database structure or permissions. This may indicate privilege abuse, lateral movement, or a compromised application account attempting escalation.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC07.name: No formal account inventory
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC07.desc: Organizations don't maintain authoritative lists of who should have database access, making dormant accounts invisible.

SEC-SQL-NET-002-RC07.name: Monitoring and Observability Tied to Defaults
SEC-SQL-NET-002-RC07.desc: Monitoring tools, dashboards, and alerting configured for default ports. Moving ports requires updating instrumentation.

SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC09.name: Incomplete Infrastructure as Code Security
SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC09.desc: Terraform, CloudFormation, or other IaC templates contain insecure defaults that weren't reviewed before deployment. Modules copied from examples without security hardening.

SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC10.name: No Network Access Control List (NACL) Restrictions
SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC10.desc: AWS/Azure network ACLs not configured to restrict database port traffic, only relying on security groups which have been misconfigured.

SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC13.name: DNS Misconfiguration
SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC13.desc: Database hostname resolved to rootcause IP address instead of private/internal DNS name, allowing uncontrolled internet access.

SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC14.name: No Default-Deny Network Policy
SEC-SQL-NET-001-RC14.desc: Organizations didn't implement zero-trust or default-deny network architectures, relying instead on security awareness to prevent unauthorized exposure.

SEC-SQL-NET-002-RC06.name: Application Connection String Hardcoding
SEC-SQL-NET-002-RC06.desc: Applications configured with connection strings pointing to default ports. Changing ports requires code changes, config file updates, and testing across all clients.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC09.name: Data exfiltration patterns in transactions
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC09.desc: Active transactions show patterns consistent with data exfiltration: large result set extractions, bulk export operations (BCP, COPY, INTO OUTFILE), linked server/foreign data wrapper queries, or systematic table-by-table reads indicating data harvesting.

SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC05.name: Permission and privilege discovery queries
SEC-SQL-AUD-010-RC05.desc: Queries against HAS_TABLE_PRIVILEGE, fn_my_permissions, SESSION_PRIVS, information_schema.role_table_grants, or equivalent reveal an account systematically mapping what it is allowed to access.

SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC01.name: Direct DML executed on audit or log tables
SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC01.desc: INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statements target known audit or log tables (AUD$, pgaudit logs, sys.fn_get_audit_file targets, mysql.general_log), indicating an attempt to modify or erase the activity record.

SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC06.name: Operating System Default Restrictions
SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC06.desc: The OS has disabled TLS 1.0/1.1 at the Schannel level (Windows registry), but the database server was installed before this change, and reinstallation is not feasible.

SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC13.name: Hybrid Cloud Connectivity
SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC13.desc: Organizations connecting on-premises databases to cloud resources via VPN or dedicated connections may leave TLS 1.0/1.1 enabled due to VPN appliance or cloud service requirements.

SEC-SQL-PAT-001-RC13.name: Lack of automatic failure during deployment processes
SEC-SQL-PAT-001-RC13.desc: No policies force systems to prevent deployment or operation on unsupported versions, allowing EOL systems to remain silently in production.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC07.name: Patch validation failures in staging
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC07.desc: Some patches fail validation in test environments, requiring investigation, vendor escalation, or workarounds that consume time and delay production deployment.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC08.name: Vendor patch delays for specific platforms or configurations
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC08.desc: Some database vendors release patches slower for specific operating systems, hardware, or cloud environments, creating unavoidable delays.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC11.name: Lack of patch rollback and recovery procedures
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC11.desc: Organizations uncertain how to safely rollback a failed patch deployment avoid patching altogether rather than risk system failure.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC10.name: Same login active from multiple hosts
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC10.desc: A single login name has concurrent active sessions originating from two or more different client hosts. This may indicate credential sharing, stolen credentials being used in parallel, or a brute-force attack that has succeeded.

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC11.name: Schema reconnaissance activity
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC11.desc: Active transactions are querying system catalogs, metadata views, or information_schema tables to enumerate database objects, columns, permissions, or configurations. This is a common first step in database attacks — mapping the target before exploitation.

SEC-SQL-PAT-001-RC08.name: Resource constraints and competing priorities
SEC-SQL-PAT-001-RC08.desc: Database teams spread thin across multiple systems lack bandwidth for planned upgrades, especially in organizations where new feature development takes precedence over maintenance activities.

SEC-SQL-PAT-001-RC10.name: Loss of institutional knowledge
SEC-SQL-PAT-001-RC10.desc: Original architects and engineers who designed the systems have left the organization, leaving no one with sufficient expertise to plan and execute complex upgrades safely.

SEC-SQL-PAT-001-RC14.name: Vendor licensing and support service uncertainty
SEC-SQL-PAT-001-RC14.desc: Organizations uncertain about licensing implications, support pricing for extended support, or cloud service EOL timelines delay decision-making. **Organizational Root Causes:** - **Absence of strategic technology refresh planning** – Organizations lack formal EOL roadmaps or capital planning processes that account for database lifecycle management as a regular operational cost. - **Siloed responsibilities across infrastructure, application development, and security teams** – No single team owns database lifecycle management, so responsibility falls through cracks with no accountability for...

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC03.name: Inadequate testing environments and procedures
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC03.desc: Organizations lack reliable staging environments that mirror production configurations, forcing teams to choose between untested deployment and delayed patching.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC04.name: Fear of patch-induced breaking changes
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC04.desc: Previous experiences with database patches introducing compatibility issues or breaking application functionality create organizational hesitation to deploy patches proactively.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC05.name: Long approval workflows and change control processes
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC05.desc: Multi-step approval hierarchies, compliance sign-offs, and change advisory board meetings delay patch deployment beyond the window of urgency.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC06.name: Resource constraints and manual patching processes
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC06.desc: Database teams cannot patch systems fast enough without automation, and lack of automation means slow, error-prone deployment.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC12.name: Critical patches for rarely-exploited vulnerabilities
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC12.desc: Organizations suffer from alert fatigue when 90% of patches address theoretical vulnerabilities; prioritization failures lead to critical patches being missed among low-risk noise.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC13.name: Incomplete patches that bypass exploits
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC13.desc: Vendors release patches that address the reported vulnerability but leave alternative attack vectors open, requiring multiple patch cycles to fully resolve an issue.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC14.name: Delayed CVE scoring and analysis
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC14.desc: The National Vulnerability Database (NVD) and vendor security advisories sometimes lag weeks behind exploit availability, leaving organizations unable to prioritize patching decisions.

SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC15.name: Patch delivery and content distribution delays
SEC-SQL-PAT-002-RC15.desc: Regional patch delivery networks or vendor infrastructure limitations delay patch availability in certain geographic locations or cloud regions. **Organizational Root Causes:** - **Reactive patching culture driven by compliance audits** – Organizations only prioritize patches when audits or regulatory reviews demand them, missing the actual threat window before patches are deployed. - **Absence of formal SLAs for critical patch deployment** – No defined targets (e.g., "critical patches within 48 hours") create ambiguity about urgency and accountability. - **Organizational unwillingness to...

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC04.name: Certificate Signed with Weak Hash
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC04.desc: SSL/TLS certificates are signed with MD5 or SHA-1 instead of SHA-256, representing a legacy certificate that has never been replaced.

SEC-SQL-ENC-004-RC01.name: Feature Not Enabled at Backup Time
SEC-SQL-ENC-004-RC01.desc: Backup procedures do not include the encryption option. Each vendor requires vendor-specific syntax or tools for backup encryption, and organizations use default backup commands without enabling it.

SEC-SQL-VS-001-RC14.name: Complexity in multi-cluster environments
SEC-SQL-VS-001-RC14.desc: MC's ability to manage multiple clusters with different security configurations creates inconsistent privilege enforcement across the infrastructure

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC12.name: Dormant account suddenly active
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC12.desc: An account that has had no login activity for an extended period (30+ days) is now executing transactions. Dormant accounts that suddenly become active are high-risk indicators of credential compromise or unauthorized reactivation.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC01.name: Installation of untrusted procedural languages
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC01.desc: Extensions like plpythonu, plperlu, and pljavaU allow arbitrary code execution with superuser privileges, creating direct OS-level attack vectors

SEC-SQL-ENC-004-RC10.name: Certificate and Key Expiration on Backups
SEC-SQL-ENC-004-RC10.desc: Backup encryption certificates or keys expire, and the organization did not renew them before expiration. Backups taken after certificate expiration may be unrestorable.

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC03.name: Deprecated Algorithm Still in Use
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC03.desc: The organization is using older encryption algorithms (Blowfish, DES, SHA-1) that were appropriate when configured but have since been deprecated due to known vulnerabilities, and the configuration has never been updated.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC03.name: Lack of extension vetting before installation
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC03.desc: Administrators install extensions without reviewing source code, checking CVE databases, or understanding security implications

SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC13.name: Mass data modification in transactions
SEC-SQL-ACC-010-RC13.desc: Active transactions are performing bulk UPDATE or DELETE operations affecting a large number of rows. This may indicate ransomware activity, data sabotage, unauthorized data manipulation, or a destructive script running against production.

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC05.name: Extensions can CREATE OR REPLACE existing objects
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC05.desc: Malicious actors can plant objects that extensions will adopt and grant superuser privileges to, enabling privilege escalation

SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC10.name: No automated vulnerability scanning
SEC-SQL-VS-002-RC10.desc: Absence of tools to scan installed extensions against CVE databases or security advisories leaves known vulnerabilities undetected

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC10.name: CBC Mode Still Allowed in Configuration
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC10.desc: Cipher suites using CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) mode are allowed, which are vulnerable to specific attacks (BEAST, padding oracle). AEAD modes (GCM) are preferred but not enforced.

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC11.name: TLS 1.2 Allows Weak Ciphers
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC11.desc: TLS 1.2 itself does not mandate strong ciphers; servers can negotiate weak ones. Organizations running TLS 1.2 but allowing weak cipher suites have false confidence in their security.

SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC11.name: Service account privilege excess
SEC-SQL-INJ-002-RC11.desc: SQL Server service accounts run with overly broad permissions (local admin, domain user rights); xp_cmdshell abuse leverages these excessive permissions.

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC13.name: Asymmetric Key Weak Parameters
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC13.desc: RSA keys used for encryption or digital signatures use key sizes below 2048 bits, or Elliptic Curve keys use weak curves.

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC12.name: Key Rotation Policy Not Implemented
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC12.desc: Encryption keys have never been rotated, and weak keys from the initial setup remain in use years later. There is no process to retire old keys and generate new ones.

SEC-SQL-AUD-020-RC01.name: Database or schema dropped (audit trail)
SEC-SQL-AUD-020-RC01.desc: A DROP DATABASE / DROP SCHEMA (SQL Server) or DROP PLUGGABLE DATABASE / DROP TABLESPACE (Oracle) was recorded in the audit trail within the last 24 hours.

SEC-SQL-AUD-004-RC01.name: Logging level set to "Errors Only"
SEC-SQL-AUD-004-RC01.desc: The logging verbosity is too low, capturing only system critical errors but ignoring authentication failures (which are often treated as "warnings" or "info").

SEC-SQL-AUD-020-RC02.name: Table dropped (audit trail)
SEC-SQL-AUD-020-RC02.desc: A DROP TABLE statement was recorded in the audit trail within the last 24 hours, on any table.

SEC-SQL-AUD-020-RC03.name: User, login or role dropped (audit trail)
SEC-SQL-AUD-020-RC03.desc: A DROP USER / DROP LOGIN / DROP ROLE statement was recorded in the audit trail within the last 24 hours.

SEC-SQL-AUD-020-RC04.name: Data deleted from a table (audit trail)
SEC-SQL-AUD-020-RC04.desc: A DELETE or TRUNCATE TABLE statement was recorded in the audit trail within the last 24 hours, on any table.

SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC02.name: Audit settings disabled or downgraded mid-session
SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC02.desc: Commands such as ALTER SYSTEM SET log_statement=none, NOAUDIT, sp_configure audit level changes, or SET GLOBAL general_log=OFF are issued during an active session, reducing the audit coverage for subsequent actions.

SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC03.name: Audit or log table truncated or dropped
SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC03.desc: A TRUNCATE or DROP statement targets an audit, log, or event-history table, destroying the evidentiary record of prior database activity.

SEC-SQL-AUD-021-RC01.name: Successful database authentication events captured
SEC-SQL-AUD-021-RC01.desc: Confirms DBDOME captures successful database logons (authentication events) across all supported engines: reads the live current-session view (V$SESSION / dm_exec_sessions / pg_stat_activity / PROCESSLIST / syssessions) and, on Oracle & SQL Server, also the audit trail of successful logons. Verify by simply logging in to the database.

SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC04.name: Trigger disabled immediately before DML operation
SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC04.desc: An ALTER TABLE DISABLE TRIGGER or equivalent command is issued within the same session shortly before a DML statement on the same table, bypassing row-level audit or validation logic.

SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC05.name: Error log or event buffer cleared during session
SEC-SQL-AUD-011-RC05.desc: Commands such as sp_cycle_errorlog, ALTER SYSTEM SWITCH LOGFILE, FLUSH LOGS, or DBMS_SYSTEM.KSDWRT are executed, rotating or clearing the server error log to remove evidence of prior errors or suspicious activity.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC10.name: Assume-inside-firewall security model
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC10.desc: Configuration assumes all network clients are trusted because they're "inside the firewall," enabling OS auth without additional controls.

SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC09.name: No centralized policy definition
SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC09.desc: In multi-database environments, each database has different policies or none at all, with no central enforcement mechanism.

SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC01.name: Transaction open beyond threshold with no activity
SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC01.desc: A session has an active transaction that has not been committed or rolled back for longer than a configurable threshold (e.g. 30 minutes) with no recent query activity, suggesting an abandoned, stuck, or deliberately held transaction.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC11.name: LDAP with weak connection security
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC11.desc: LDAP authentication for databases configured over unencrypted connections, allowing credential interception and replay.

SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC07.name: Configuration file permission bypass
SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC07.desc: Administrators create accounts with empty passwords intentionally to store credentials in secured configuration files, believing the file permissions compensate for null passwords.

SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC02.name: Exclusive locks held on large tables for extended period
SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC02.desc: A session holds exclusive or access-exclusive locks on tables with a significant row count for an unusually long time, blocking other operations and potentially indicating intentional lock-based denial of service.

SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC09.name: Application provisioning defaults
SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC09.desc: Application deployment frameworks automatically create database accounts with empty passwords if password parameters are omitted in templates.

SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC10.name: LDAP/directory integration incomplete
SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC10.desc: Organizations planning to use LDAP authentication create database accounts with null passwords until LDAP integration is completed, but integration is never finished.

SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC11.name: Batch user creation scripts
SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC11.desc: DBA scripts for bulk account creation use empty passwords as placeholders expecting them to be changed later, but cleanup never happens.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC12.name: No OS authentication logging
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC12.desc: Database logs don't capture details about OS authentication source, making audits of remote OS auth impossible.

SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC12.name: No pre-deployment security scanning
SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC12.desc: Accounts with empty/null passwords are not detected by deployment validation tools before the environment goes live.

SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC01.name: Default configuration never modified
SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC01.desc: Databases ship with minimal or no password complexity requirements, and administrators never configure stronger policies after installation.

SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC03.name: Legacy system requirements
SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC03.desc: Old applications cannot handle special characters or uppercase/lowercase requirements, so weak policies are set to accommodate legacy apps.

SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC07.name: User friction avoidance
SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC07.desc: DBAs and admins reduce complexity to minimize support calls and password reset requests, prioritizing convenience over security.

SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC03.name: Idle-in-transaction session blocking downstream operations
SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC03.desc: A session in the idle in transaction state is holding locks that are blocking a queue of other waiting sessions, a pattern associated with application bugs, connection pool exhaustion, or deliberate resource starvation.

SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC13.name: Account creation automation without validation
SEC-SQL-AU-003-RC13.desc: Scripts that create accounts batch-mode use weak password templates without policy enforcement.

SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC04.name: Large-volume rollback indicating probe-and-revert behaviour
SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC04.desc: A transaction that modified a large number of rows is rolled back, with the same pattern repeated multiple times within a session, consistent with an attacker probing data constraints or testing injection payloads without committing.

SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC06.name: Kerberos/SSPI authentication without encryption
SEC-SQL-AU-004-RC06.desc: Windows SSPI or Kerberos authentication enabled remotely but without requiring channel encryption, assuming token freshness equals authentication security.

SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC10.name: Account privilege escalation over time
SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC10.desc: Default admin accounts are initially left "for testing" but become production accounts as applications depend on them, and nobody revisits the decision.

SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC12.name: Assumption of "unused" protection
SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC12.desc: DBAs believe unused accounts don't pose risk if network access is restricted, overlooking lateral movement threats within the network.

SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC03.name: Installation interruption
SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC03.desc: Installation processes that require password entry for admin accounts may be skipped or terminated early, leaving accounts with null passwords.

SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC04.name: Test account forgotten in production
SEC-SQL-AU-002-RC04.desc: Temporary test accounts created with blank passwords during development are not removed before promotion to production.

SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC03.name: Database not in protected network
SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC03.desc: Assumption that the database is internal-only. Default accounts are left active because administrators believe external access is restricted, creating a false sense of security.

SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC07.name: Recovery procedure reliance
SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC07.desc: Some DBAs intentionally leave default accounts enabled to have a recovery path if regular admin accounts are locked out or credentials are lost.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC14.name: Audit trails insufficient
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC14.desc: Login auditing doesn't capture enough detail to distinguish "never used since creation" from "used once years ago."

SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC09.name: No integration with identity provisioning
SEC-SQL-AU-001-RC09.desc: Default accounts are not tracked in identity access management systems, making them invisible to access reviews and governance processes.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC02.name: Offboarding process incomplete
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC02.desc: When employees depart, access removal is assigned but not verified to completion; accounts remain active indefinitely.

SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC05.name: Savepoint abuse with repeated partial rollbacks
SEC-SQL-AUD-012-RC05.desc: A session creates and rolls back to savepoints in rapid repeated cycles, which is abnormal application behaviour and may indicate automated probing of data state or attempts to exploit MVCC timing windows.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC03.name: Service account lifecycle unknown
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC03.desc: Service accounts created for applications/integrations are never tracked; when the application is decommissioned, the account persists.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC01.name: Misunderstanding of rootcause role scope
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC01.desc: Administrators do not fully understand that permissions granted to rootcause automatically apply to every user on the database, including future users and accounts they do not intend to provision.

SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC02.name: Administrator convenience during setup
SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC02.desc: DBAs enable `trust` authentication temporarily for initial setup and testing (to avoid password requirements), then forget to disable it.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC04.name: Contractor account cleanup forgotten
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC04.desc: Temporary contractor or vendor accounts created with expiration dates, but expiration is not enforced; accounts become dormant.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC05.name: Temporary project access never revoked
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC05.desc: Database accounts created for specific projects are marked as temporary but never removed after project completion.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC09.name: Quarterly reviews too infrequent
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC09.desc: Access reviews happen once per year or less; accounts can be dormant for months before detection.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC10.name: Shared service accounts misclassified
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC10.desc: Accounts used by applications are treated as user accounts; when applications are decommissioned, accounts are forgotten.

SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC09.name: Configuration Oversight
SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC09.desc: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 were disabled in registry/config by security hardening scripts but the database server was not restarted, or configuration was done on some nodes in a cluster but not all.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC08.name: HR/Identity integration absent
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC08.desc: No integration between HR/identity systems and database access management; terminated employees' database accounts are not automatically disabled.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC12.name: No automated dormancy detection
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC12.desc: Database tools that identify unused accounts aren't deployed or their reports aren't acted upon.

SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC13.name: Privilege accumulation over time
SEC-SQL-AU-006-RC13.desc: Dormant accounts often retain elevated privileges from their original roles; privilege isn't reduced just because the account is unused.

SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC09.name: Recovery procedure reliance
SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC09.desc: DBAs intentionally keep `trust` for loopback to recover from lost superuser passwords, not recognizing container/VM host access risks.

SEC-SQL-NET-002-RC05.name: Port Scanning Facilitation
SEC-SQL-NET-002-RC05.desc: Well-known ports make automated port scanning trivial. Attackers immediately know where to find services without port discovery phase.

SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC12.name: Administrator password forgotten or locked
SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC12.desc: When the superuser password is lost and the account is locked, `trust` mode becomes an unintended recovery path that's never cleaned up afterward.

SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC02.name: Deprecated Client Libraries in Use
SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC02.desc: Applications use SQL Native Client, OLEDB (SQLOLEDB), or other deprecated database drivers that only support TLS 1.0/1.1 and cannot be upgraded due to application vendor end-of-life.

SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC01.name: Security-relevant ALTER SYSTEM or SET executed by non-admin
SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC01.desc: A non-superuser or non-DBA account issues ALTER SYSTEM, SET SESSION, or sp_configure commands that change authentication, SSL, logging, or access-control parameters, undermining the server security posture.

SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC04.name: Development environment settings
SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC04.desc: Database in development or testing uses permissive authentication (no password required) for ease of access; settings are replicated to production via configuration management without security review.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC02.name: Quick-fix troubleshooting approach
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC02.desc: When specific users report permission errors, administrators grant the required permission to rootcause rather than identifying and fixing the actual required privilege for the specific user or role.

SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC05.name: Remote access addition overlooked
SEC-SQL-AU-007-RC05.desc: When remote access is enabled on the database, the existing permissive local authentication rules are not replaced with password-based or certificate-based rules, allowing any user on localhost to connect without credentials.

SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC02.name: Principle of least privilege not enforced
SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC02.desc: No governance mechanism ensures users have only the minimum permissions needed for their tasks, allowing administrative privileges to accumulate beyond necessity.

SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC02.name: Dangerous feature enabled during session
SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC02.desc: Commands enabling xp_cmdshell, UTL_FILE directory access, DBMS_SCHEDULER OS jobs, or LOAD DATA INFILE are issued during an active session, opening OS-level execution vectors from within the database.

SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC03.name: Trigger disabled or dropped on monitored table
SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC03.desc: ALTER TABLE DISABLE TRIGGER, DROP TRIGGER, or equivalent commands target tables that carry audit, validation, or row-history triggers, removing controls that enforce data integrity or change tracking.

SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC04.name: Audit or logging parameters changed mid-session
SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC04.desc: Session-level commands reduce or disable query logging, error reporting, or audit verbosity (e.g. SET log_min_duration_statement=-1, NOAUDIT ALL, SET GLOBAL slow_query_log=OFF), creating a blind spot for subsequent activity.

SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC06.name: Multi-schema and cross-database application requirements
SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC06.desc: Applications that legitimately access multiple schemas or databases across the database server are granted elevated privileges rather than being re-architected with explicit per-object permissions.

SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC08.name: Absence of periodic access reviews and certification
SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC08.desc: No formal process exists to regularly audit who has administrative privileges, why they have them, and whether the justification still applies.

SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC09.name: Employee role transitions without privilege adjustment
SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC09.desc: When employees change roles or responsibilities, their old administrative privileges are not revoked, creating accumulation over time.

SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC12.name: Vendor default configurations
SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC12.desc: Database installations from major vendors ship with default accounts and elevated privilege structures; these are not hardened during initial setup.

SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC13.name: No centralized identity and access governance
SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC13.desc: Database access is managed independently from enterprise identity systems (Active Directory, LDAP), creating silos where cross-system privilege consistency cannot be enforced.

SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC14.name: Shared service and application accounts
SEC-SQL-AZ-001-RC14.desc: Multiple applications or users share single accounts with elevated privileges, making it impossible to attribute actions and enforce individual least privilege.

SEC-SQL-CFG-005-RC05.name: Dangerous Flag Combinations
SEC-SQL-CFG-005-RC05.desc: Multiple trace flags enabled over time; combination of flags creates unexpected behaviors or conflicts not documented

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC04.name: Legacy database practices
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC04.desc: Older database installations had rootcause granted broad permissions to simplify management; these permissions were never audited or removed during subsequent upgrades.

SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC05.name: Network or authentication configuration modified at runtime
SEC-SQL-AUD-013-RC05.desc: Commands that alter pg_hba.conf, firewall rules, linked-server definitions, or remote authentication providers are issued at runtime, potentially opening new access paths that bypass existing controls.

SEC-SQL-AUD-014-RC01.name: New user or login created during application session
SEC-SQL-AUD-014-RC01.desc: A CREATE USER, CREATE LOGIN, or CREATE ROLE statement is executed during what appears to be a normal application session, indicating possible backdoor account creation for persistent re-entry.

SEC-SQL-AUD-014-RC02.name: Account added to privileged role mid-session
SEC-SQL-AUD-014-RC02.desc: A GRANT ROLE, ALTER SERVER ROLE ADD MEMBER, or GRANT DBA command elevates an existing account to a highly privileged role (sysadmin, DBA, superuser) outside of a formal change-management process.

SEC-SQL-AUD-014-RC03.name: Password changed on another account during active session
SEC-SQL-AUD-014-RC03.desc: An ALTER USER ... PASSWORD or equivalent command changes the credential of an account other than the currently logged-in user, potentially resetting a dormant account for re-activation.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC05.name: Insufficient permission auditing on rootcause
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC05.desc: No regular reviews occur to audit what permissions rootcause currently holds and whether those permissions align with organizational security policies.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC06.name: Default view permissions in system objects
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC06.desc: Many databases grant rootcause SELECT on system views and metadata tables by default; administrators extend this to user tables without recognizing the risk.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC07.name: Confusion between schema and database-level rootcause
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC07.desc: Administrators may grant specific intended permissions at one level but not fully understand the inheritance and scope across the entire database or server.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC08.name: Testing/development configuration copied to production
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC08.desc: Development or test databases grant rootcause broad access for convenience; these configurations are replicated to production without review.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC09.name: Bulk permission scripts without proper restriction
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC09.desc: Configuration management scripts or deployment automation grant permissions at scale without explicit filtering to exclude rootcause.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC10.name: Lack of role-based alternative
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC10.desc: No well-defined roles for common user categories exist; instead of creating "read-only_users" or "application_readers" roles, administrators grant rootcause permissions.

SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC11.name: Incompletely implemented permission revocation
SEC-SQL-AZ-002-RC11.desc: Attempts to restrict rootcause permissions fail or are incomplete; revocation statements have syntax errors, incomplete scope, or are not applied to all objects.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC01.name: Absence of user lifecycle management automation
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC01.desc: Organizations lack formal processes or tools to automatically deprovision accounts when employees leave, contractors end engagements, or systems are decommissioned.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC08.name: Shared database accounts and credentials
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC08.desc: Multiple users share a single database account (often through shared passwords), making it impossible to identify which accounts can be safely removed without disrupting someone's work.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC04.name: Lack of integration between HR systems and database access
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC04.desc: Database access is not synchronized with the authoritative source of truth for employee status (HR system, LDAP, Active Directory); when an employee is terminated in HR, the database account is not automatically disabled.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC05.name: No reconciliation process between database accounts and authorized users
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC05.desc: No regular audit compares accounts in the database against the current roster of employees and contractors; dormant and orphaned accounts are never identified.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC06.name: Service and application accounts without ownership tracking
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC06.desc: Accounts created for applications, batch jobs, or services lack clear ownership documentation; when an application is decommissioned, no one knows which database accounts to remove.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC07.name: Contractor and vendor accounts without explicit end dates
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC07.desc: Third-party accounts are created without documented expiration dates; they persist indefinitely even after the contractor relationship ends.

SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC11.name: No Automated Configuration Audit
SEC-SQL-ENC-002-RC11.desc: There is no recurring audit or monitoring to detect when TLS 1.0/1.1 becomes enabled via patches, configuration drifts, or application updates.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC09.name: Cross-database and application account complexity
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC09.desc: Users have accounts across multiple databases and systems; when they leave, accounts in some systems are deprovisioned while others are forgotten.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC10.name: Legacy account creation without documentation
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC10.desc: Accounts created many years ago lack ownership documentation or audit trails; administrators cannot determine why they exist or who should use them.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC11.name: Database environment fragmentation
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC11.desc: Organizations maintain multiple database environments (production, staging, development) with separate account management; accounts in lower environments are never cleaned up.

SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC05.name: Self-Signed Certificates with Weak Parameters
SEC-SQL-ENC-005-RC05.desc: Self-signed certificates were generated with weak parameters (1024-bit RSA, SHA-1 signature) using command-line defaults instead of explicit strong key specifications.

SEC-SQL-AZ-004-RC05.name: Default configuration not hardened during installation
SEC-SQL-AZ-004-RC05.desc: Database installations use default settings that do not restrict file operations; these defaults are not changed during initial setup.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC13.name: Application default accounts never updated
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC13.desc: Applications ship with default service accounts that are provisioned but never changed; when applications are decommissioned, these accounts remain.

SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC15.name: Assumption that low-privilege accounts are harmless
SEC-SQL-AZ-003-RC15.desc: Orphaned read-only accounts are left active because they are perceived as low-risk; this creates an expanded attack surface and complicates audit trails.

SEC-SQL-AZ-004-RC02.name: Lack of secure alternatives or awareness of alternatives
